We study whether a frontier large language model, used as a coding agent with open-source tools only, can match them in quality and speed. We report every run, and independent checkers verify every schedule. On the 100,000-operation job shop tai_100_1000_1, an agent-written solver reached 525,515, below OptalCP, Hexaly, and CP Optimizer. Unchanged, it improved all ten instances of the family and closed two. With equal budgets on the same workstation, it ended 0.0-1.8% above the lower bound, against 2.6-5.8% for CP Optimizer and 2.4-4.4% for Hexaly. On the Behnke-Geiger flexible job shops, an agent-written tabu search improved 11 of 32 open instances. With two transport robots, an agent-written solver improved seven of ten MKT instances. New lower bounds show that four published MKT values cannot be attained on the distributed instance files. Agent-run improvement campaigns closed eight further instances.
papers.comments: 27 pages, 4 figures, 14 tables. Submitted to International Transactions in Operational Research. Data, schedules, checkers and code: https://github.com/andrealbrechtl/agent-heuristics-jobshop-supplement/

papers.title: delta-Derivations of Finite-Dimensional Simple Lie Algebras with Values in Arbitrary Modules
papers.abstract: We determine the spaces of \(δ\)-derivations of finite-dimensional complex simple Lie algebras with values in arbitrary modules for \(δ\ne0,1\). In rank at least two, these derivations vanish unless \(δ=\frac{1}{2}\), in which case they are precisely the module homomorphisms from the adjoint module. For \(\mathfrak{sl}_2\), we characterize the derivation spaces in terms of Casimir eigenspaces and determine when they are nonzero. When the coefficient module is simple, every nonzero derivation module is simple except possibly at \(δ=2\), where it has a simple essential socle with a finite-dimensional semisimple quotient. We describe these modules via translation functors and give explicit formulas for the derivations.

papers.title: Semistable 1-Motives: Monodromy, Explicit Periods, and Local Duality
papers.abstract: Let $K/\mathbf Q_p$ be unramified, with $p>2$. For a $1$-motive with constant lattice, split torus, and good abelian quotient, we compute the semistable extension complex from toric valuations and formal-group logarithms. A canonical monodromy boundary exists for every semistable representation; it detects splitting over crystalline periods and the increase in monodromy rank. For the stated $1$-motives, this boundary and the unramified quotient recover the restricted local Tate pairing, with exponential radicals. Nonsplit elliptic examples, Raynaud uniformization, and a height-one positive-period bound explain the geometric range. For toric motives we construct actual periods, convergent Robba bases, and integral action matrices. A toric basis family has perfect projective/trace-zero matrix duality, including its exact integral defect. An explicit residue-zero solution operator constructs every dual Herr class. Applied componentwise, the same operator gives relative full dual lifts for general constant-lattice $1$-motives once their coefficient sequence is specified. Finally, finite-base coefficient traces realize division-tower Iwasawa cohomology for any Tate lattice, and the period cup pairing equals the arithmetic group-ring pairing.

papers.title: Co-rotating and traveling asymmetric vortex sheets for the planar Euler equation
papers.abstract: The aim of this paper is to construct co-rotating and traveling vortex sheet pairs with asymmetric configurations for the two-dimensional incompressible Euler equation. The vorticity of these solutions is concentrated on two small closed curves of different sizes, which carry vortex sheets of different circulations and either rotate uniformly about their centroid or translate with constant speed. The proof relies on the Birkhoff--Rott formulation of the problem and on the implicit function theorem at the point vortex pairs.

papers.title: Admissible Yang--Baxter equation for Nijenhuis perm superalgebras
papers.abstract: We develop a superization of the theory of admissible Yang--Baxter equations for Nijenhuis perm algebras initiated by Ma and Song. We introduce Nijenhuis perm superalgebras, their representations, and the dual representation, with Koszul signs chosen so that the contraction of the Yang--Baxter tensor matches the $\mathcal O$-operator equation exactly. We define Nijenhuis perm superbialgebras and characterise them by matched pairs. In the coboundary case, we show that every even supersymmetric solution of the $S$-admissible perm Yang--Baxter equation gives rise to a Nijenhuis perm superbialgebra, and we give sufficient conditions for a perm superalgebra to admit a Nijenhuis operator constructed from such a solution. Examples with purely odd components illustrate the role of the grading.

papers.title: Numerical verification for harmonic maps: Counterexamples to Eells' conjecture
papers.abstract: This paper develops a framework to construct harmonic maps $S^3 \rightarrow S^2$ numerically, which is used to construct approximate harmonic maps in homotopy classes with Hopf invariant $2,3,4,5,6$. By using a rigorous fixed-point argument, it is shown that there exist genuine harmonic maps with the same Hopf invariant close to these approximate solutions, thus producing a family of counterexamples to Eells' conjecture, and the related Ding's conjecture.

papers.title: A Unified Framework for First- and Second-Order Energy-Stable Parametric Finite Element Methods for Planar Willmore Flow
papers.abstract: The construction of structure-preserving schemes for planar Willmore flow that are second-order accurate in time and avoid large coupled nonlinear solves remains challenging. In this work, we develop a unified framework for first- and second-order fully discrete energy-stable parametric finite element schemes for planar Willmore flow with a length-penalization term. The framework is based on a new equivalent reformulation involving a global auxiliary variable. The main novelty lies in the second-order construction, which combines midpoint curvature quantities weighted by elementwise arc-length Jacobian ratios with a compatible discrete tangent to obtain exact discrete chain rules for the bending energy and curve length. A further contribution is to show that both schemes satisfy discrete modified energy dissipation laws that yield the same type of a priori bounds on the discrete solution as the original energy law. They also retain Barrett--Garcke--N{ü}rnberg tangential motion to promote favorable mesh distribution. Each stage reduces to two linear solves with exactly the same coefficient matrix and one scalar nonlinear solve. We rigorously prove unique solvability of the linear subproblems under suitable assumptions and derive computable sufficient conditions for local existence and uniqueness of the scalar solution near unity. Numerical experiments demonstrate the expected temporal accuracy, energy dissipation, good mesh quality and computational efficiency.

papers.title: General linear groups in tangent categories
papers.abstract: General linear groups are well-studied Lie groups that encode the linear symmetries of a finitely-dimensional linear space. In differential geometry, they are an important ingredient of various constructions, including fibre bundles and the frame bundle of a principal bundle. They also appear in algebraic geometry as affine group schemes. Their Lie algebra, known as the general linear Lie algebra, is isomorphic to the Lie algebra of square matrices, whose Lie bracket is given by the commutator. Building on previous work on Lie groups, in this paper we introduce general linear group objects in the context of tangent categories. We define the general linear group of a differential object as a classifier of the Kleisli parametrized linear automorphisms of the differential object, a class of maps that generalize linear automorphisms in a suitable sense. We prove that such a group can be entirely constructed via a tangent triple equalizer and use this characterization to prove that the Lie algebra of general linear group objects is isomorphic to the Lie algebra of linear endomorphisms.

papers.title: Refined random matrix conjectures for zeros of $p$-adic $L$-functions
papers.abstract: We make and test the conjecture that for $p$-adic $L$-functions associated to quadratic Dirichlet characters and their Teichmüller twists, all local statistics of zeros in the unit disk match those of $p$-adic random matrix eigenvalues. This generalizes the case of the number of zeros in the unit disk previously conjectured by Ellenberg-Jain-Venkatesh, which was well-supported by numerics, as well as the case of the discriminant, where their numerics were more ambiguous. Using recent random matrix results on local statistics of eigenvalues, we make the random matrix prediction explicit for many statistics, analogous to local densities and pair-correlations in the complex setting. To test these, we compute data on $p$-adic $L$-functions for characters of conductor up to $10^7$, and for certain statistics in windows above $10^{10}$. We find good agreement with the new random matrix predictions for these statistics, as well as for the discriminant.
papers.comments: 68 pages, 12 figures. Supplementary file data_supplement.pdf contains all averages plotted on these figures. Code used for p-adic L-function computations is available at https://github.com/knospe/iwasawa-power-series

papers.title: Online Carbon-Aware Power Flexibility Quantification of Distributed Data Centers
papers.abstract: Geographically distributed data centers (DCs) can provide spatio-temporal power flexibility to electric grids through the coordinated management of computing resources and energy. Beyond their energy consumption, the carbon footprints of DCs are non-negligible, which constrain the power flexibility that DCs can offer to the power grid. To address this challenge, this paper proposes a carbon-aware power flexibility quantification framework for DCs. We first develop an optimization model that characterizes DC power flexibility in a grid-usable form, namely the Cartesian product of adjustable power demand intervals across time slots. An online algorithm based on Lyapunov optimization is then designed to solve the flexibility quantification model in real time under uncertain workload arrivals and fluctuating grid carbon intensity. Furthermore, an integrated disaggregation and feedback mechanism is devised to translate the power system operator's dispatch commands into real-time DC operating decisions and to capture their impact on future DC flexibility. Several desirable properties of the proposed model and method are proven, including disaggregation feasibility, bounded workload processing delays, and a bounded suboptimality gap. Numerical simulations demonstrate that our approach effectively unlocks DC power flexibility while satisfying carbon emission constraints, outperforming baseline algorithms.

papers.title: Cubic local observability of Gaussian-blind sources in thermal $φ^4_2$ fields
papers.abstract: We study external sources that are invisible to a spatially local observation in a massive Gaussian thermal field on a circle. A quadratic-reference calibration removes the first-order thermal mass-shift signal. For the resulting quartic model we prove a cutoff-independent, source-uniform $C^1$ expansion of local Wick cubic means. Its leading operator has the time-integrated cube of the thermal covariance as its kernel. A positive bilateral Laplace representation proves injectivity on the entire external source space, while analyticity gives exponential singular-value upper bounds. The expansion yields local Araki relative-entropy lower bounds on every fixed finite-dimensional source space, and a uniform separation theorem at every prescribed Sobolev resolution. Under an additional interval-length condition, a reflection-positivity identity yields an explicit, nonoptimal double-logarithmic conditional stability bound for this specific thermal kernel. Continuum probability estimates and the integrability assumptions of the Feynman--Kac--Nelson construction are verified in Section~3.

papers.title: The non-stationary $\widehat{\mathfrak{gl}}_N$ affine Laumon function and its difference equation
papers.abstract: We present an explicit $q$-Givental type formula for the $\widehat{\mathfrak{gl}}_N$ non-stationary affine relativistic Toda or affine Laumon function introduced by Shiraishi. We prove the conjecture of [J. Shiraishi, Affine screening operators, affine Laumon spaces and conjectures concerning non-stationary Ruijsenaars functions. J. of Int. Systems, 4 (2019)], that this function obeys a non-stationary difference equation involving an operator $\widehat{\mathcal T}$, which represents a quiver automorphism (Dehn twist) of the quantum cluster algebra of the affine $A_{N-1}^{(1)}$ Q-system.

papers.title: Proximal Adam algorithm for nonsmooth composite optimization and linear convergence under proximal PL geometry
papers.abstract: We analyze Adam-type methods for nonsmooth composite optimization problems $\min_xΦ(x)=f(x)+h(x)$, where $f$ is smooth and $h$ is convex, proper, and lower semicontinuous. The nonsmooth term is treated by a metric-weighted proximal map, while the smooth term is preconditioned by the Adam second-moment matrix. We prove a composite descent lemma whose constants depend explicitly on the spectral bounds of the adaptive metric and a residual--step equivalence that converts proximal step decay into subgradient stationarity. These yield an $O(1/N)$ bound on the minimum proximal stationarity residual for the deterministic proximal normalized gradient method without convexity of $f$, and the same $O(1/N)$ rate for proximal Adam under quantitative momentum-alignment and residual-coherence conditions together with a metric-compatibility condition. By estimating the momentum error directly, the same $O(1/N)$ rate is also obtained without the momentum-alignment and residual-coherence assumptions. When the composite objective satisfies a proximal Polyak--Łojasiewicz inequality, both algorithms and the relaxed proximal Adam scheme converge linearly with explicit contraction factors. Numerical experiments on a diagonal Lasso problem, two-dimensional image TV denoising, and two-dimensional elastic parameter identification illustrate the predicted stationarity and linear rates.

papers.title: Rigidity for pivotal braided r-categories of moderate growth and applications to vertex operator algebras
papers.abstract: Let $\mathcal{C}$ be an abelian pivotal braided r-category with simple unit object $\mathbf{1}$ over any field. We present a ChatGPT-generated proof, prompted by Bin Gui, that any object $X$ in $\mathcal{C}$ of moderate growth, in the sense that $\dim\mathrm{End}(X^{\otimes n})<n!$ for some $n\in\mathbb{Z}_{\geq 1}$, is rigid. The proof crucially uses ideas from the recent proof of Etingof and Penneys that $X$ is rigid if it is also non-negligible, that is, $X\otimes Y$ contains $\mathbf{1}$ as a direct summand for some object $Y$. In the present paper, the non-negligible assumption is removed using a rigidity criterion developed previously by the author for use in non-semisimple categories. We also present a variant result (found without further AI assistance) that $X$ is also rigid if $\dim\mathrm{Hom}((DX)^{\otimes n}\otimes X^{\otimes n},\mathbf{1})<n!$ for some $n\in\mathbb{Z}_{\geq 1}$, where $D$ is the Grothendieck-Verdier duality functor of $\mathcal{C}$. Using this variant, we show that if $V$ is a simple self-contragredient vertex operator algebra such that the category $\mathcal{C}^1_V$ of $C_1$-cofinite grading-restricted generalized $V$-modules is closed under contragredient modules, then $\mathcal{C}^1_V$ is a locally finite $\mathbb{C}$-linear abelian rigid braided ribbon category. We also show that if $V$ is a simple $\mathbb{Z}_{\geq 0}$-graded self-contragredient $C_2$-cofinite vertex operator algebra, then the category of all grading-restricted generalized $V$-modules is a (not necessarily semisimple) modular tensor category.

papers.title: Global generation of coinvariant vector bundles on $\overline{\mathrm{M}}_{0,n}$
papers.abstract: Using fusion closed-ness and strong generation properties, we identify collections of modules over vertex operator algebras (VOAs) whose induced vector bundles of coinvariants on the moduli space $\overline{\mathrm M}_{0,n}$ of stable $n$-pointed curves of genus zero are globally generated. These results specialize to \cite{Fak12} for affine VOAs at positive integer levels, and of \cite{DG23} for strongly rational VOAs that are generated in degree 1. To illustrate the results, and to show that fusion-closedness is essential, we give numerous examples, including Lattice VOAs, Simple Current Extensions of Affine VOAs, and various tensor products.

papers.title: High-probability convergence of adaptive, proximal, and clipped Adam-type methods for nonconvex stochastic optimization
papers.abstract: This paper develops a unified high-probability analysis of adaptive, proximal, and clipped first-order methods for nonconvex stochastic optimization. For a smooth objective whose stochastic gradient error has sub-Gaussian norm, the normalized adaptive gradient method attains the standard stochastic nonconvex complexity of the square root of the number of iterations, with an additional logarithmic dependence on the inverse confidence level that is inversely proportional to the number of iterations. The proof uses an adaptive descent decomposition together with Freedman and Bernstein concentration inequalities. The same guarantee is established for the full adaptive moment method under an explicit momentum-alignment condition. The analysis is extended to projected and proximal updates through a stationarity measure based on the subdifferential distance, to objectives satisfying the Polyak-Lojasiewicz condition, and to heavy-tailed noise through truncation. The framework is applied to stochastic inverse problems in elasticity, and numerical experiments illustrate the theoretical scaling and the practical behavior of the methods.

papers.title: Minimaxity in Robust Nonparametric Regression: from Heavy-Tailed to Sub-Gaussian Assumptions
papers.abstract: We study nonparametric regression over star-shaped function classes under strong adversarial contamination. The clean (original) observations $(\tilde{X} _{i},\tilde{Y} _{i})_{i=1} ^{n}$ are i.i.d. and satisfy $\tilde{Y} _{i}=f ^{*}(\tilde{X} _{i})+ξ_{i}$, where $f ^{*}\in \mathcal{F}$, $\tilde{X}$ is distributed as $\mathbb{P} _{X}$, and the noise is conditionally centered. An adversary may inspect the clean sample and replace at most $\lfloor εn\rfloor$ observation pairs. We assume that $\mathcal{F}\subset L _{2}(\mathbb{P} _{X})$ is star-shaped with finite diameter $d$. Under a Bernstein-type moment condition on function increments and a bounded conditional second moment for the noise, we establish the matching lower and upper bounds of order $\left((η^{*}) ^{2} \vee ε\right)\wedge d ^{2}$, uniformly over admissible star-shaped function classes, therefore characterizing the minimax rate of estimation error, where \begin{equation*} η^{*}:=\sup\left\{η>0: nη^2\leq\log \mathcal M _{\mathcal{F}}^{\text{loc}}(η,c)\right\}. \end{equation*} Here $\log \mathcal{M} _{\mathcal{F}} ^{\text{loc}}(η,c)$ denotes the local metric entropy of $\mathcal{F}$ in $L _2(\mathbb{P} _{X})$, and $c$ is a sufficiently large constant. Under a uniform relative sub-Gaussian condition on function increments and noise, the lower bound is adjusted to $\left((η^{*})^{2}\vee ε^{2}\right)\wedge d ^{2}$ while the upper bound improves to $\left((η^{*})^{2}\vee ε^{2}\log ^{2}\left(\frac{e}{ε}\right)\right)\wedge d ^{2}$, yielding minimax optimality up to logarithmic factors.

papers.title: The Polyak-Łojasiewicz Paper: A 10-Year Retrospective
papers.abstract: In 2016, we wrote a paper introducing the phrase "Polyak-Lojasiewicz (PL) condition" for an old idea, unsure of how readers would react. The paper ultimately had a larger impact than we expected, and we are surprised and honoured to receive the 2026 PKDD ECML Test of Time Award. With 10 years of hindsight, this note offers an informal and candid retrospective on the PL condition. We take a look back at the origins of the paper, give an AI-assisted refined version of the main theorem, review criticisms of the work, and discuss a variety of related ideas and extensions.

papers.title: Exponential Double and Multiple Riordan Arrays as Fiber Products
papers.abstract: A double Riordan array has nonzero entries only in positions $(n,k)$ with $n+k$ even, and its even and odd parts are Riordan arrays with the same multiplier function. We develop this observation systematically, with the emphasis on exponential double and exponential multiple Riordan arrays. Using generalized Riordan arrays with respect to a sequence $(c_n)$, we show that the double Riordan group, the exponential double Riordan group, the multiple Riordan group, and the exponential multiple Riordan group are fiber products of (generalized) Riordan groups over the Lagrange group. For exponential double and exponential multiple Riordan arrays this yields product and inverse formulas without square or $\ell$th roots, valid over any field of characteristic zero; an abelian normal subgroup with quotient the Lagrange group and a corresponding splitting; subgroups isomorphic to the Riordan group; an iterated split-extension description of the multiple groups; and a characterization of elements of finite order, including the fact that over ${\mathbb R}$ every element of finite order is an involution. We show that the $\ell$th power of the production matrix is the direct sum of the production matrices of the compressions, give an explicit formula for it in terms of partial Bell polynomials, and characterize these arrays by a shared $A$-sequence. Finally, we reverse the construction. Two Riordan arrays with a common multiplier can always be interleaved into a unique double Riordan array, and into an ordinary Riordan array exactly when their first functions satisfy one more condition. Examples include Pascal-, Catalan-, Morgan--Voyce-, and ballot-type arrays.

papers.title: One-bubble stability, reduced coefficients, and threshold compactness for the Escobar functional
papers.abstract: Let $(M^n,g)$ be a smooth compact manifold with nonempty boundary and coercive conformal energy. For $n\ge5$, in a conformal representative with $H_g=0$, we prove quantitative stability near a concentrating boundary bubble whose center stays away from the umbilic locus. The norm of the constrained gradient controls the distance to the standard bubble family with sharp exponent $1/2$, and the distance to the Lyapunov--Schmidt corrected family linearly. In the same one-bubble neighborhood, at energies at least the sharp hemisphere value $S_\ast$, the distance to the standard family is also controlled linearly. These estimates follow from the exact reduced quadratic coefficient and the scale-derivative expansion of the reduced functional. The same scale equation shows that sequences of critical points at $S_\ast$ can concentrate only at umbilic points. For $n\ge3$, a profile decomposition without a sign assumption gives Palais--Smale compactness between $S_\ast$ and the first mixed level $(S_\ast^{n-1}+Y^{n-1})^{1/(n-1)}$, where $Y=C^*_{\text{Esc}}(M,g)$, and this endpoint is sharp. Between $S_\ast$ and the two-bubble level, we characterize noncompact levels by the lower critical values. For $n\ge7$, we obtain the fourth-order reduced expansion at umbilic centers. Under local total umbilicity, we evaluate the correction exactly, determine the conformal weight of the reduced coefficient, and obtain the optimal algebraic comparison with the squared ambient Weyl norm.
papers.comments: 57 pages. Split from arXiv:2601.22665v2 (Part 2/3). Final part forthcoming. Comments welcome!

papers.title: Convergence analysis of physics-informed neural networks for subdiffusion
papers.abstract: Physics-informed neural networks have emerged as mesh-free solvers for partial differential equations, yet their rigorous convergence theory for time-fractional problems remains limited. We present a convergence analysis of PINNs for linear subdiffusion equations and for the associated backward problem of recovering the initial data from terminal observations. To address the nonlocality and weakly singular kernels of fractional derivatives, we introduce a discretization-based PINN framework built on some popular time-stepping schemes satisfying discrete maximal regularity, including backward Euler, BDF2, L1, and fractional CN schemes. This approach avoids the exact evaluation of fractional derivatives at training points while preserving the stability structure needed for convergence analysis. For the forward problem, we prove that, under the natural fractional maximal-regularity condition $u\in W^{α,p}(0,T;L^2(Ω))\cap L^p(0,T;H^2(Ω)\cap H_0^1(Ω))$, the piecewise linear temporal reconstructions of PINN-loss minimizers converge to the exact solution. This result avoids the higher-order regularity assumptions on the exact solution that are often imposed in existing PINN convergence analyses. We also verify the required discrete maximal regularity and consistency properties for the aforementioned popular time discretizations. We then extend the analysis to the backward subdiffusion problem and establish convergence of the regularized recovery of the initial data from terminal observations, despite its ill-posedness. Numerical experiments for both forward and backward problems support the theoretical results, demonstrate the necessity of regularization, and show that $L^2$-type losses alone are generally insufficient. These results establish a rigorous theoretical basis for discretization-based PINNs for time-fractional diffusion problems.

papers.title: Rational lines on pairs of quadrics and cubic hypersurfaces
papers.abstract: We study rational lines on smooth intersections of two quadrics and on smooth cubic hypersurfaces over number fields. For an intersection of two quadrics in $n$ variables, we prove the Hasse principle and weak approximation for the variety of lines when $n\geq 11$, and more generally for the variety of $r$-planes when $n\geq 3r+8$. In this range an $r$-plane exists over the ground field if and only if one exists over every real completion. For the variety of lines, we also prove the Hasse principle and weak approximation when $n\geq 8$, conditional on the finiteness of certain Tate-Shafarevich groups. For a smooth cubic hypersurface in $n$ variables, we prove that a line exists over the ground field when $n\geq 23$.

papers.title: Toward the Minimal Set of Information Inequalities in Regenerating Codes: An Algebraic Approach
papers.abstract: Information-theoretic outer bounds for exact-repair regenerating codes can be formulated as linear programs, but the associated Shannon-type systems contain many implicit equalities and redundant inequalities. We directly specify a reduced system for the $(n,n-1,n-1)$ exact-repair model using the closure structure induced by its repair dependencies. Nonempty closed sets index the reduced joint-entropy coordinates, and inseparable edges determine the defining inequalities. We prove equivalence with the initial system by characterizing its implicit equalities and establishing sufficient redundancy criteria. We also give an algorithm that constructs the directly defined system for any $n$, count its entropy coordinates, and derive an explicitly computable upper bound on its number of inequalities. For every $n\ge2$, we prove that the reduced system has no implicit equalities and that each distinct defining inequality is nonredundant and defines a facet in the nonempty closed-set coordinate space. Exact enumerations for $n\in\{2,3,4,5\}$ verify the reported system sizes.

papers.title: Compatible by Construction: Bottom-Up Nonlinear Model Reduction without Interface Bases
papers.abstract: Nonlinear manifolds can provide compact representations of solutions to partial differential equations (PDEs), but generating training data and learning these representations on large domains remain costly. We present a bottom-up framework that reuses local nonlinear representations learned on a small training domain to solve larger PDE systems. A shared nonlinear decoder represents the full set of degrees of freedom owned by each subdomain, without separate interior and interface models. Each global degree of freedom has a unique owner, and local residuals directly use decoded state values from the corresponding neighboring subdomains. The resulting discrete state is single-valued by construction, eliminating the need for independent interface copies and additional interface compatibility constraints. Physical coupling is retained through the original time-discrete PDE residual. With the decoder held fixed, the subdomain-specific reduced coordinates are determined jointly by minimizing this residual, and the Gauss--Newton system is assembled from local contributions. Experiments on parameterized viscous Burgers and incompressible Navier--Stokes problems demonstrate reuse on larger domains without retraining. Comparisons with local proper orthogonal decomposition models under the same coupling construction show favorable accuracy--efficiency trade-offs in the tested regimes.

papers.title: Exceptional sequences of line bundles on $\mathrm{Fl}(1,\ell;\ell+1)$
papers.abstract: Let $X_\ell=\mathrm{Fl}(1,\ell;\ell+1)\subset\mathbb{P}^\ell\times(\mathbb{P}^\ell)^\vee$ be the incidence variety of points and hyperplanes in $\mathbb{P}^\ell$. We prove that for every $\ell\ge 3$, every exceptional sequence of line bundles on $X_\ell$ of maximal length $\ell(\ell+1)=\operatorname{rk} K_0(X_\ell)$ is full. Together with the case $\ell=2$, due to Altmann, Hochenegger and Witt, this shows that for all $\ell\ge2$ an exceptional sequence of line bundles on $X_\ell$ is full if and only if it has maximal length. The proof translates exceptionality into a combinatorial condition on lattice points of $\operatorname{Pic}(X_\ell)\cong\mathbb{Z}^2$ and reduces fullness to sequences containing a non-orthogonal descent. A capacity count for admissibly ordered subsets rules out all but one family of descents; for that family we classify the possible configurations and verify generation using Euler sequences and Koszul complexes.

papers.title: Entire curves in surface bundles over tori
papers.abstract: Cattalani recently initiated the study of Ahlfors currents in symplectic topology. We combine these with the symplectic pairs of Bande-Kotschick to show that some non-trivial surface bundles over tori have pseudoholomorphic entire curves. In particular the Kodaira-Thurston manifold has an entire curve for every $J$ tamed by an invariant form.

papers.title: Domains of attraction of quasi-stationary distributions for an absorbed random walk
papers.abstract: We study a continuous-time random walk on the positive integers, killed at zero, where the downward rate $a$ and upward rate $b$ satisfy $a>b>0$. Its quasi-stationary distributions form a one-parameter family. We show that if the initial distribution $(m_n)_{n\geq 1}$ is strictly positive and satisfies $m_{n+1}/m_n\to r$, where $(b/a)^{1/2}<r<1$, then its conditional distribution given survival converges in total variation to the corresponding nonminimal quasi-stationary distribution. We obtain asymptotic equivalents for the joint probabilities of position and survival, and for the survival probability itself. We also give a moment condition under which the minimal quasi-stationary distribution is selected. Finally, we construct an initial distribution whose successive-term ratios do not converge but whose conditional distribution nevertheless converges to a nonminimal quasi-stationary distribution. Thus the ratio condition is sufficient but not necessary.

papers.title: The Dirichlet Problem for Quaternionic $k$-Hessian Equations
papers.abstract: We study the Dirichlet problem for quaternionic $k$-Hessian equations on smooth bounded domains. For a smooth positive density $f(q,z)$ satisfying $f_z\ge0$, we prove existence and uniqueness of a smooth admissible solution whenever a smooth admissible subsolution with the prescribed boundary values exists. The proof extends the quaternionic Monge--Ampère subsolution method to $2\le k<n$ through boundary second derivative estimates. We also construct subsolutions on strictly quaternionic $(k-1)$-convex domains and characterize smooth solvability for constant boundary values.

papers.title: Localization for Lipschitz monotone quasi-periodic operators with power-law hopping
papers.abstract: We prove spectral and dynamical localization for quasi-periodic operators on $\mathbb Z^d$ with Lipschitz monotone potentials and power-law hopping. For sufficiently small coupling, localization holds at every allowed phase whenever the hopping decay exponent $r$ exceeds the Diophantine exponent $τ$. The proof is based on multiscale analysis with exponentially growing scales. We use homotopy in the coupling constant to select the local eigenvalue branches and Schur complement estimates to control the successive elimination of coordinates.

papers.title: Closed formulas for the permanents of structured matrices
papers.abstract: We give finite formulas for permanents of structured matrices and prove polynomial bounds for their evaluation. Over any field, the permanent of a matrix of bounded rank-width can be computed from the matrix alone, answering a question of Lyaudet. In characteristic $p>0$, the bound is $p^{O(k)}n^{O(1)}$, where $k$ is the rank-width. In characteristic zero, a determinant formula treats Cauchy matrices with an added polynomial of fixed degrees in the row and column nodes. This includes polynomial perturbations of Hilbert matrices and dense Toeplitz and Hankel families. For ordered cuts we give a single determinant; in positive characteristic, rational diagonal sequences give a fixed rational generating function for the Toeplitz permanents. We also give formulas for cycle weights and hook immanants. For translation matrices we obtain signed determinant formulas and classify the supports for which the permanent is the coefficientwise absolute value of the determinant. Further formulas cover cyclic block matrices, residue supports, and bands bounded on one side.

papers.title: An accelerated multiobjective gradient flow with implicit Hessian-driven damping
papers.abstract: In this paper, we propose an accelerated multiobjective gradient flow with implicit Hessian-driven damping for unconstrained convex multiobjective optimization problems in a real Hilbert space. The continuous flow is formulated as a system of two first-order equations involving only a single multiobjective projection operator and suitable time-scaling factors. Formally, it can also be expressed as a second-order system with explicit multiobjective Hessian-driven damping, which corresponds to the usual Hessian-driven damping introduced by Alvarez et al. [J. Math. Pures Appl., 81(8):747--779, 2002]. The first-order formulation, however, involves no Hessian term and can be regarded as an extension of the Hessian-driven Nesterov accelerated gradient flow by Chen and Luo [arXiv:1912.09276, 2019]. Assuming that the objective gradients are Lipschitz continuous on bounded sets and that the common lower level sets are bounded, we establish global existence in finite dimensions under suitable time-scaling conditions. An a priori energy estimate confines the solutions to a fixed bounded set, and a Lyapunov argument yields fast decay of a merit function and the KKT residual. Under an additional bound on the time-scaling factors, the trajectory of every global solution converges weakly to a weak Pareto point. Numerical tests illustrate the rapid residual decay and reduced oscillations.

papers.title: Contractions of realizations and differential invariants of the algebra sl(2,C)
papers.abstract: In this paper, we formalize a method for constructing limit transitions between local realizations of Lie algebras based on contractions of the corresponding algebras. In the complex holomorphic category, contractions of faithful realizations of the special linear algebra sl(2, C) to the complex three-dimensional Poincaré algebra and the Weyl-Heisenberg algebra are explicitly constructed. For the contraction of a generating realization of the algebra sl(2,C) to the algebra g_{3.4}^{-1}, differential invariants are constructed and a limit system of Newtonian type is found.

papers.title: Weighted Euler transforms, real-rootedness, and $γ$-positivity
papers.abstract: For $a>0$ and a polynomial $F$ of degree $m$, let $H_{a,F}$ denote the weighted Euler numerator of $F$, defined as the numerator of the generating function $\sum_{k\ge0}(a)_kF(k)x^k/k!$ with denominator $(1-x)^{a+m}$. For every $a>0$, we show the following preservation result: if the numerators $H_{a,F}$ and $H_{a,G}$ have only real nonpositive zeros, then the same holds for $H_{a,FG}$. The proof relies on an explicit multiplication formula in falling-factorial coordinates and a characterization of multiplier sequences for generalized Laguerre bases due to Brändén and Ottergren. Furthermore, when the symmetric degrees coincide with the ordinary degrees of the input polynomials, the same operation preserves $γ$-positivity. For positive integers $a=r$, the weight is the Ehrhart polynomial of the standard simplex $Δ_{r-1}$. This yields geometric preservation theorems for products with a single simplex factor, as well as applications to Gorenstein polytopes and a Reeve tetrahedron example.

papers.title: Inequalities for intersection numbers from Hodge-Riemann relations
papers.abstract: We derived inequalities for intersection numbers of nef classes inside algebras satisfying the Kähler package, using Hodge-Riemann relations up to degree two. As an application, we construct certain strictly Lorentzian polynomials and show that they cannot be realized as the volume polynomial of nef classes inside such an algebra.

papers.title: A Helly theorem for the Bruhat-Tits building
papers.abstract: Let $K$ be a discretely valued field with valuation ring $\mathcal{O}$. We show that a finite family of $\mathcal{O}$-lattices in $K^m$ is adapted to a common basis if any subfamily of at most $m+1$ $\mathcal{O}$-lattices is. In other words, in the Bruhat-Tits building of $\operatorname{GL}(m)$, a finite family of simplices lies in a common apartment if and only if any subfamily of at most $m+1$ simplices does. The proof uses a version of Radon's theorem for $\mathcal{O}$-lattices. We also give an alternative proof using truncated modules.

papers.title: Projective surfaces with infinite fundamental group and trivial profinite completion
papers.abstract: For every nontrivial finite abelian group \(A\) of odd order, we construct a smooth complex projective surface with infinite topological fundamental group and trivial étale fundamental group. The isomorphism types of its finite subgroups are precisely those of the subgroups of \(A\). The surface is Kobayashi hyperbolic and has Stein universal cover.

papers.title: Extreme central $L$-values of almost prime quadratic twists of elliptic curves II
papers.abstract: We prove lower bounds for central $L$-values of quadratic twists of an elliptic curve by discriminants with at most five prime factors. Under the rank-zero Birch--Swinnerton-Dyer formula, these bounds give large Tate--Shafarevich groups.

papers.title: On configurations that are nearly generalised polygons
papers.abstract: Payne (1972) introduced nearly generalised $n$-gons as $(s+1)$-regular bipartite graphs of girth $2n$ with small excess over the Moore bound. Biggs and Ito (1980) proved nonexistence of such graphs if $s > 1$ and $n > 3$, leaving open the existence of regular antipodal planes. We revisit this problem from several equivalent viewpoints. First we show that a regular antipodal plane of order $s$ is equivalent to a balanced weighing matrix whose support is the incidence matrix of a biplane with parameters \[ 2-\left(\frac{s^2+s+2}{2},\,s+1,\,2\right). \] This gives short determinant and local-arithmetic obstructions to existence. We then formulate the question of signing a biplane as an affine linear system over $\mathbb F_2$, and use this formulation to prove that no regular antipodal plane of order $s$ exists with $4\le s\le 14$. Finally, we give further equivalent formulations in terms of sharply deranged families of permutations and mutually orthogonal array-bic squares. These translations provide new computational and structural approaches to Payne's conjecture that regular antipodal planes exist only for $s=2,3$.

papers.title: Ergodicity without monotonicity: patch-positive spin systems
papers.abstract: Monotonicity is the standard tool for proving that an interacting particle system is ergodic. What can replace it when the system is not monotone and its invariant measure is unknown? The simplest such systems are kinetically constrained models such as FA-1f and East exposed to noise. In these models vacancies enable updates, so adding vacancies should help the system forget its initial state. We prove this for a broad class of spin systems, which we call patch-positive. If vacancies are created spontaneously at a uniformly positive rate, the system converges to the same equilibrium from a large class of initial states, and from every initial state if the threshold density is at most $\tfrac12$ or the interactions are oriented. In particular, the East model with noise is ergodic at every density, and we obtain new cases of the positive-rates conjecture. The key idea is to compare the dual processes of the system with and without the added deaths.

papers.title: HOL in HOL: mechanized soundness, completeness and consistency, with and without infinity
papers.abstract: What can a logic certify about a copy of itself? For Church's simple theory of types, formalized as a deep embedding in Isabelle/HOL with Henkin semantics and a natural-deduction calculus, the answer has two tiers. On the first tier, plain Isabelle/HOL certifies the logic without an axiom of infinity, by a standard model with one individual. On the second tier, the logic with a Dedekind-style axiom of infinity is certified only in Isabelle/HOL extended by a large enough set-theoretic universe. Both tiers appear in Harrison's self-verification of HOL Light. What the present formalization adds is Henkin completeness, and with it a semantics that matches the calculus exactly, compactness and model existence on the first tier, and the boundary between the tiers. Comparing two ways of adding infinity to the object logic shows where the boundary lies. One is an infinite domain of individuals, expressed by the first-order sentences "there are at least $n$ individuals", each of which has a finite model; the other is the Dedekind axiom, a single sentence with no finite model, and there the first tier ends. In the calculus the axiom is strictly stronger than the sentences together: it derives each of them, but they do not derive it. The witness is a countable Henkin model in which every sentence holds and the axiom fails, because its function domain is too sparse for an injective, non-surjective self-map. On the second tier, the universe serves one purpose only: to prove the Dedekind axiom consistent. Everything that follows, completeness and even the countable Henkin model of the axiom, is obtained in plain Isabelle/HOL. The universe axiom is Harrison-style, realized in Paulson's ZFC_in_HOL with the domain of every type in $V_{ω+ω}$; with it, full classical higher-order logic with infinity and relational choice is consistent relative to set theory.
papers.comments: 23 pages, 1 figure. Formal proof artifacts: Archive of Formal Proofs entries HOL_in_HOL_Deep and HOL_in_HOL_Deep_Infinity_ZFC (Isabelle2026). Submitted

papers.title: Goodman-type lower bounds for graph homomorphism densities
papers.abstract: For a finite graph $H$ with $v(H)$ vertices, chromatic number $χ(H)$, and chromatic polynomial $P_H$, define $Φ_H(p)=(1-p)^{v(H)}P_H((1-p)^{-1})$. This polynomial interpolates the homomorphism densities of $H$ in balanced complete multipartite graphons. We study the lower bound $t(H,W)\geΦ_H(p)$ on the homomorphism density of $H$ in graphons $W$ of edge density $p>1-1/(χ(H)-1)$, which generalises Goodman's triangle bound. We prove the inequality for chordal graphs whose maximal cliques have equal size, for trivially perfect graphs, and for joins of a clique and an odd cycle. The proofs use entropy along clique trees and a convexity criterion for adding a universal vertex. We also prove that a nonbipartite graph satisfies the inequality at all sufficiently high edge densities if and only if its girth is odd. For a graph on $n$ vertices whose girth is odd, the bound holds whenever $p>1-(72n^{12})^{-1}$. The proof combines Whitney's forest expansion with a spectral comparison of cycle densities. Finally, among the $117$ nonbipartite graphs on at most six vertices with no isolated vertices or isolated edges, exactly $94$ satisfy the bound. The main results are formally verified in Lean 4.

papers.title: Non-vanishing of central $\rm GL_3$ L-values in the level aspect
papers.abstract: We study non-vanishing of central standard $L$-values of spherical cuspidal $\mathrm{GL}_3$ newforms of prime level. A logarithmic Möbius mollifier with finite inverse Euler factors, combined with a conjugate term from the functional equation, gives a non-vanishing harmonic proportion of at least $1/2-\varepsilon$ for every $\varepsilon>0$ and all sufficiently large prime levels. The required mixed moment is evaluated by an asymmetric approximate functional equation.

papers.title: Fano-Enriques threefolds of Fano index $>1$
papers.abstract: We study $\mathbb{Q}$-Fano threefolds of Fano index greater than $1$ whose Weil divisor class group has nontrivial torsion. We give a complete list of their possible numerical types: there are $176$ of them, which refine to $182$ possible graded Hilbert series. At least $40$ numerical types are realised: $27$ by quotients of weighted complete intersections by cyclic groups, twelve by quotients of threefolds of codimension $4$ or $5$ and one by a quotient of the del Pezzo threefold of degree $5$. Seventy-two numerical types are shown not to occur. In particular the torsion subgroup need not have prime order, and the Weil and $\mathbb{Q}$-Fano indices can be $(1,2)$, $(1,3)$ or $(1,4)$.

papers.title: Chow Stability of Polarized K3 Surfaces with ADE singularities
papers.abstract: The asymptotic Chow stability of smooth polarized K3 surfaces is known through the existence of Ricci-flat metrics and Donaldson's theorem. We give a purely algebraic proof and extend the result to polarized K3 surfaces with at worst ADE singularities. The proof gives a uniform effective bound for the exponent, depending only on the degree of the polarization. Following the approach of Mumford and Morrison, we establish quantitative estimates for linear systems and their contributions to Chow weights, without restrictions on the Picard number.

papers.title: The speed of convergence for propagation of chaos in the mean-field Ising model
papers.abstract: We derive sharp relative-entropy asymptotics for increasing propagation of chaos in the Curie--Weiss model at zero external field. For every fixed inverse temperature $0<β<1$, the relative entropy of a $k$-spin marginal with respect to the symmetric product measure is $$ \frac{β^2}{4(1-β)^2}\frac{k(k-1)}{N^2}+o\left(\frac{k^2}{N^2}\right),\qquad k=o(N). $$ At the critical inverse temperature $β=1$, the rate changes to $α_{\mathrm c}^2 k(k-1)/(4N)+o(k^2/N)$ in the regime $k=o(\sqrt N)$, where $α_{\mathrm c}$ is the second moment of the limiting quartic law of the rescaled magnetization. We also obtain asymptotics for sequences $β_N\uparrow1$ that interpolate between these two regimes. Crucially, the proof reveals that the pair correlations determine the leading correction to the likelihood ratio, providing precise control of both the chi-square divergence and relative entropy.

papers.title: Existence and uniqueness of non negative radial solutions to semilinear elliptic problems on the exterior of a unit ball in $\mathbb{R}^2$
papers.abstract: We study the problem \begin{equation}\notag \begin{cases} - Δu &= λK(x) f(u) \hspace{.1cm} \mbox { in } B_1 ^c, \\ u(x)&=0 \hspace{1.5cm} \mbox { on } \partial B_1, \end{cases} \end{equation} where $λ$ is a positive parameter, $B_1^c:=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^2:|x|>1\}$ is the exterior of the unit ball in $\mathbb{R}^2$, $K:B_1^c\rightarrow (0,\infty)$ is a $C^1$ radial function and $f:[0,\infty)\rightarrow \mathbb{R}$ is a $C^1$ concave function which is sublinear at infinity such that $f(0)<0$. We establish the existence and uniqueness of non negative radial solutions for large values of parameter $λ$. Moreover, we prove certain qualitative properties of nonnegative radial solutions for a class of problems in dimension 2. In contrast to the case $n\geq3$, where positive solutions decay to zero at infinity, we prove that non negative solutions are positive, radially increasing with the limit existing at infinity.

papers.title: High-Dimensional Gaussian and Bootstrap Approximation: Near $1/\sqrt{n}$ Rates with General Covariance
papers.abstract: We consider Berry-Esseen bounds over rectangles for sums of $n$ random vectors in $\mathbb{R}^p$ that are i.i.d. A longstanding open question in high-dimensional probability and statistics is whether bounds of order $1/\sqrt n$ are attainable up to factors of $\log(pn)$ when the population covariance matrix is unrestricted. We answer this question affirmatively, provided that the random vectors have sub-Gaussian entries with non-zero variance. In addition, we provide analogous results for bootstrap approximation and Gaussian comparison, which make use of a special discrepancy measure between covariance matrices that enables improvement with respect to prior work. Taking an approach based on interpolation, the novel aspects of the proofs deal with bounding the interpolation derivatives in a way that is not sensitive to the covariance structure.

papers.title: A solution to Petty's polar projection problem
papers.abstract: In 1971, Petty asked whether a convex body in $\mathbb{R}^n$, $n\geqslant 3$, must be an ellipsoid if its projection body is a dilate of its polar. In this paper, we give an affirmative answer to this question.

papers.title: Statistical guarantees for signature kernel ridge regression
papers.abstract: Path signatures are a standard tool for learning functionals on path space. The main underpinnings of their application are universal approximation results. For a wide range of function classes on path space, these results state that any function in such a class can be approximated arbitrarily well by a linear functional of the path signature. Hence, linear functionals of the signature are in principle expressive enough for learning functions on path space. Nonetheless, these results do not provide insights into the statistical question of how much data is needed to identify a suitable signature functional. In this work, we study this question in the framework of kernel ridge regression with the signature kernel. The target is the conditional expectation $\E[Y|X]$, where $X$ is the observed path and $Y$ is a real-valued response. Under different assumptions on the moments of the signature kernel and the response, we provide finite-sample and consistency guarantees for the method. We supplement our theoretical analysis with numerical experiments that illustrate our results.
papers.comments: Keywords: Path space regression, Signature transform, Rough paths, Functional data analysis, Kernel methods

papers.title: Projection of massive and interacting conformal theories to the future null infinity
papers.abstract: On a four-dimensional, globally hyperbolic and asymptotically flat spacetime, we consider a real, linear, massive scalar field. Within the framework of perturbative algebraic quantum field theory and inspired by the principle of perturbative agreement, we regard the mass term in the underlying Lagrangian as an interaction potential. This allows us to construct the algebra of observables of the massive theory and, using a Møller map, to represent its elements as formal power series in the squared mass, with coefficients in the algebra of observables of a massless, conformally coupled scalar field. Following [DMP06], we use the bulk-to-boundary correspondence for the massless theory to project each coefficient to future null infinity $\mathscr{I}^+$.In four-dimensional Minkowski spacetime, we prove convergence of the projected series in the presence of an infrared cut-off and show that the global adiabatic limit exists but is trivial. We circumvent this obstruction by exploiting the time-slice axiom, which allows us to restrict our attention to observables localized in a causally convex neighbourhood containing a Cauchy hypersurface. Removing the cut-off locally yields a non-trivial limit and hence a bulk-to-boundary correspondence for the massive theory. We then extend our procedure to a self-interacting real scalar field. We represent interacting observables as formal power series in the coupling constant, with coefficients in the algebra of observables of a massless, conformally coupled scalar field. Each coefficient in the domain of the bulk-to-boundary map can thus be projected to future null infinity. As a concrete example, we apply this method to the stress-energy tensor of a massless scalar field with a quartic self-interaction, computing its projection up to first order in perturbation theory.

papers.title: A narrow band method for non-causal discretizations of anisotropic eikonal equations, with adaptive width, sub-and super-solution construction, and quasi-linear complexity
papers.abstract: We describe a narrow band method for numerically solving anisotropic eikonal equations, and more generally static first order Hamilton-Jacobi equations with possibly non-convex Hamiltonians, discretized using standard schemes (semi-Lagrangian, upwind-differences, Lax-Friedrichs). The causality property is not needed, in contrast with the fast marching method. The proposed approach simultaneously builds a numerical sub-solution u and super-solution u to the problem, and adapts the width of the narrow band based on their comparison. We prove that (1 + $ε$)u $\ge$ u at termination, where $ε$ > 0 is any given tolerance parameter, and that the worst case complexity is O(N | ln $ε$| ln(N/$ε$)), where N denotes the number of discretization points, and the underlying constant is explicit in terms of those associated with the scheme properties. Numerical experiments illustrate our results.

papers.title: Auto-conditioned Gradient Descent Methods for Multiobjective Optimization
papers.abstract: This paper proposes two linesearch-free algorithms based on steepest descent methods for smooth multiobjective optimization: auto-conditioned steepest descent method for multiobjective optimization (AC-SDM) and auto-conditioned normalized gradient descent method for multiobjective optimization (AC-NGDM). Both algorithms estimate the local Lipschitz constant from the function values and the first-order information obtained in previous iterations. AC-SDM uses a shared estimate of the Lipschitz constant to construct a scaled steepest descent direction. For AC-NGDM, we use each function's local Lipschitz estimate to normalize the gradient of the corresponding function and construct the descent direction. We prove that every accumulation point of any sequence generated by both algorithms is a Pareto critical point. We also establish convergence rates of $O(1/\sqrt{k})$ for nonconvex objectives and $O(1/k)$ for convex objectives. Numerical results on several test problems demonstrate that AC-SDM and AC-NGDM require fewer iterations and less CPU time than the multiobjective steepest descent method with an Armijo line search and a max-type nonmonotone line search.

papers.title: Common values of linear recurrences related to Ankeny-Brauer-Chowla polynomials
papers.abstract: Let $P_u(X)=XQ(X)(X-u)+1$, where $Q(X)\in \mathbb{Z}[X]$ is monic, separabel, has constant term $\pm 1$, and degree $q\ge 1$. Denote $(A_n(u))$ the linear recursive sequence having characteristic polynomial $P_u(X)$ and initial terms $A_0,\ldots,A_{q+1}\in \mathbb{Z}$ such that at least one of them is non-zero. Then there exist effectively computable constants $n_0,u_0$ depending only on $Q(X)$ and $\max\{|A_0|,\ldots, |A_{q+1}|\}$ such that if $|A_n(u)| = |A_m(u)|$ holds for some integers $u,n,m$ with $u>u_0$ and $n\not=m$ then $\max\{

papers.title: Lower bounds on ranks of universal quadratic forms through geometry-of-numbers
papers.abstract: We obtain lower bounds for the ranks of universal forms over totally real cubic fields using techniques from geometry-of-numbers and the parametrisation of cubic rings by binary cubics due to Delone--Faddeev. Additionally, our methods give lower bounds for totally real primitive fields of any degree with codifferent generated by a totally positive element.

papers.title: Exponential Lower Bounds for the Spherically Averaged Density of Atoms
papers.abstract: We study the asymptotic behavior of the spherically averaged density $\widetilde ρ$ for fermionic bound states of the $N$-electron atomic Hamiltonian $H_{N,Z}$ with nuclear charge $Z$. For the density associated with an eigenfunction satisfying $H_{N,Z}ψ=Eψ$, we show that if the energy $E$ is below the bottom of the essential spectrum $Σ:=\inf\mathop{\rm ess.spec} (H_{N,Z})$, then \[ \lim_{r\to\infty}\frac{\ln \widetilde ρ(r)}{r} =\lim_{r\to\infty}\frac{d}{dr}{\ln \widetildeρ(r)} =-2α_0, \] with $α_0=\sup\{α\ge 0\colon e^{2αr}\widetilde ρ\in L^1(\mathbb{R_+},r^2dr)\}$. The same is true at threshold in certain cases. Moreover, we prove $α_0^2=Σ-E$ for the ground states of $H_{3,Z}$ with sufficiently large $Z$.

papers.title: Wireless Node Ranking via Fourier-Driven Maximum-Likelihood Estimation (extended version)
papers.abstract: We apply non-abelian Fourier theory to the problem of maximum-likelihood estimation of the order of a line topology, based on signal strength measurements under shadowing only. This yields up to a 60-fold speedup over standard methods for uncorrelated shadowing. Moreover, for correlated Gaussian shadowing with a singular covariance (e.g. the joint path-loss model), maximum-likelihood recovery is exact and independent of the shadowing variance (an infinite Le Cam threshold), which our implementation confirms for $σ/α$ as high as 7.0. The key object is the covariance's null space. Its dimension is fixed by the topology; its orientation depends on the correlation function only through the per-link variances. Although the mechanism formally requires an exact line, it is robust to small perturbations of the formation: an approximate kernel recovers as well as the exact one. We explore the dependence on the perturbation in detail for five nodes.

papers.title: The Train Unit Shunting Problem with Service Scheduling and Workforce Assignment: classical and quantum optimization approaches
papers.abstract: Efficient railway rolling stock management requires the coordinated planning of train-unit assignment, shunting movements, track occupation, service operations, and workforce allocation. These interdependent decisions give rise to a challenging combinatorial optimization problem, particularly as the size of the fleet and the planning horizon increase. This paper introduces the Train Unit Shunting Problem with Service Scheduling and Workforce Assignment, a mixed-integer linear programming formulation that integrates these operational decisions within a unified optimization framework. To improve computational tractability, a preprocessing procedure is developed to reduce the size of the resulting model. The proposed approach is evaluated through computational experiments on instances of increasing size and under different objective-function weight and cost configurations. Classical optimization experiments using Gurobi show that filtering method reduces the number of decision variables and constraints, while its impact on computational time varies across instances. In addition, a constrained quadratic model representation is investigated using D-Wave's hybrid quantum-classical optimization solver.
papers.comments: Train Unit Shunting Problem, Railway Optimization, Mixed-Integer Linear Programming, Quantum Annealing, Hybrid Quantum-Classical Optimization

papers.title: On character conductors and Sylow p-subgroups
papers.abstract: Let $P\in\operatorname{Syl}_p(G)$, where $G$ is a finite group and $p$ is a prime, and let $χ\in\operatorname{Irr}(G)$. In 2024, I. M. Isaacs and G. Navarro asked whether the degree of $\mathbb{Q}_{p^f}$ over $\mathbb{Q}_p(χ_P)$ is always at most the $p$-part $χ(1)_p$ of $χ(1)$, where $p^f$ is the $p$-part of the conductor of $χ$ and $f\geq1$. Here $\mathbb{Q}_n=\mathbb{Q}(e^{2πi/n})$ is the $n$th cyclotomic field, $χ_P$ is the restriction of $χ$ to $P$, and $\mathbb{Q}_p(χ_P)$ is the field generated over $\mathbb{Q}_p$ by the values of $χ_P$. We prove that this inequality holds for $p$-solvable groups.

papers.title: Essential spectrum of singularly perturbed Dirac operators on bounded domains
papers.abstract: In this paper self-adjoint Dirac operators on bounded domains in $\mathbb{R}^2$ and $\mathbb{R}^3$ with elliptic boundary conditions perturbed by singular $δ$-shell potentials supported on compact curves or surfaces are considered. While the unperturbed operator has purely discrete spectrum, it is shown that certain critical values of the interaction strengths lead to the appearance of essential spectrum. More precisely, each connected component of the interaction support, where the coupling constants have such critical values, produces in dimension two a point and in dimension three even a closed interval in the essential spectrum, where the size of the latter depends on the geometry and the coupling constants.

papers.title: Additive cubes are avoidable over $\{0,1,2,3\}$, $\{0,1,4\}$ and $\{0,2,5\}$
papers.abstract: We prove that additive cubes are avoidable over the alphabet $\{0,1,2,3\}$, thereby solving a long-standing question initiated by Pirillo and Varricchio in 1994. By extending the reduction and spectral machinery of Cassaigne, Currie, Schaeffer, and Shallit (2014), we prove that the search for additive cubes in such morphic images reduces to a finite graph traversal. We exhibit eight explicit morphisms from $\{0,1,3,4\}^*$ to $\{0,1,2,3\}^*$ of length 3 whose images on the Cassaigne \textit{et al.} infinite word contain no additive cubes.

papers.title: Dimensionalities on monoids
papers.abstract: We study equivalence relations on monoids in $\Rel$ that are lax morphisms. We call them \emph{dimensionalities}. We prove that the quotient of a monoid in $\Rel$ by a dimensionality is again a monoid. We prove that polygroupoids (and hence hypergroups) are exactly the symmetric $†$-Frobenius structures in $\Rel$. We use this characterization to prove that the quotient of a polygroupoid by a dimensionality that preserves the inverse is a polygroupoid.

papers.title: Existence and regularity for a non-autonomous Born-Infeld equation with a confining potential
papers.abstract: We study the non-autonomous Born-Infeld equation $\operatorname{div}(Du/\sqrt{1-|Du|^2})-V(x)u+|u|^{p-2}u=0$ in $\mathbb R^N$, where $N\ge3$ and $2<p<2^*=2N/(N-2)$. For a $C^1$ potential satisfying $\inf V>0$, $V(x)\to\infty$ as $|x|\to\infty$, and $|x\cdot\nabla V(x)|\le C_DV(x)$ with $0\le C_D<p-2$, we prove the existence of a positive classical solution and infinitely many distinct nontrivial classical solutions. The argument combines the nonsmooth monotonicity trick with compactness induced by the confining potential. A Pohozaev-type identity yields uniform bounds for parameter-dependent critical points. A local minimization characterization identifies these critical points with weak solutions and establishes strict spacelikeness. Local Schauder estimates then give $C^{2,α}_{\mathrm{loc}}$ regularity. All the solutions belong to the natural energy space $H_V^1(\mathbb R^N)$ and satisfy $|Du|<1$.

papers.title: Higher derived limits, Kurepa families and Chang's Conjecture
papers.abstract: We investigate the interplay between homological algebra and combinatorial set theory, specifically focusing on the (non)vanishing of higher derived limits of certain inverse systems of abelian groups, denoted $\mathbf C_{[κ]^λ}$, indexed by the ordered sets $([κ]^λ,\subseteq)$, where $λ< κ$ are infinite cardinals. Our first main result is a general structural theorem which provides a generalisation of Goblot's theorem to the setting of locally small directed sets. We then present the first systematic study of generalised cofinal Kurepa families. We establish their existence in the constructible universe $L$ and under specific cardinal arithmetic hypotheses. Then, we apply our structural result to show that $\mathrm{lim}^{n+2} \mathbf{C}_{[κ]^{\aleph_n}} = 0$ in environments where the appropriate cofinal Kurepa families exist. In contrast, we explore conditions that force these derived limits to be nonzero. In particular, we prove that certain instances of Chang's conjecture (CC), together with the existence of suitable $\diamondsuit$ sequences, imply that $\mathrm{lim}^{n+2} \mathbf{C}_{[κ]^{\aleph_n}} \neq 0$ for appropriate values of $κ$. Adapting forcing techniques from Eskew and Hayut, we construct models of these instances of CC together with the required $\diamondsuit$ sequences, establishing the consistency, for each $n \in \mathbb{N}$, of $\mathrm{lim}^{n+2} \mathbf{C}_{[\aleph_{ω_n}]^{\aleph_n}} \neq 0$.

papers.title: Stable projective immersions of Kähler metrics with some radial symmetry
papers.abstract: We combine Calabi's criterion with Pringsheim's theorem to study projective inducibility under positive rescaling. By restricting to suitable radial holomorphic curves, we obtain an obstruction to local Kähler immersions into finite- or infinite-dimensional complex projective space that applies uniformly to every positive rescaling. For invariant rational curves, we show that non-rationality of the moment map implies that no positive rescaling is projectively induced. We apply these criteria to the Taub-NUT, Candelas-de la Ossa, non-flat Stenzel, and Hwang-Singer scalar-flat metrics, as well as to Gibbons-Hawking metrics. Except for the Burns-Simanca metric in the Hwang-Singer family, no positive rescaling is projectively induced. For Gibbons-Hawking ALE spaces with at least two centres, the conclusion holds in every compatible complex structure. We also extend the results to complex space forms of arbitrary curvature with at least one finite signature index.

papers.title: Two correlation scales in homogeneous density-matrix functionals: the Müller logarithm and the sharp Csányi--Arias asymptotics
papers.abstract: We resolve the exact high-density correlation scales and coefficients of the three-dimensional translation-invariant, spin-symmetric Müller and Csányi--Arias corrected Hartree--Fock (CHF) functionals, settling long-standing numerical observations of Müller overcorrelation and apparently vanishing CHF correlation. In Hartree units, for fixed spin multiplicity $q$ and Fermi momentum $k=(6π^2ρ/q)^{1/3}$, their gains per particle over the filled Fermi sea satisfy \[ D_{\rm M}(k)=\frac{3}{4π^2}\log k+O(1),\qquad D_{\rm CHF}(k)=12e^{-1/2-π^2/8} k^2e^{-π^{3/2}\sqrt{k}}(1+o(1)). \] The Müller proof retains the occupation cap and identifies the factor-of-two cancellation between exchange defect and energy gain. For periodic Müller jellium, convexity and translation--spin averaging allow a global minimizer to be chosen invariant and identify the unrestricted thermodynamic energy with the homogeneous spin-symmetric value. The CHF upper bound follows from a deterministic comparison built from the explicit Hartree--Fock dispersion, combining a full Birman--Schwinger bound with one-sided norms and completion of the square; a number-preserving trial state provides the matching lower bound, and the retained remainder yields weighted $L^2$ convergence of the occupation defect without analyzing the self-consistent gap. We also prove existence for both functionals and uniqueness of the CHF minimizer. Relative to the unpolarized quantum high-density benchmark, Müller has a larger logarithmic coefficient, providing quantitative evidence for the conjectured Müller lower-bound property, whereas CHF misses the logarithmic scale altogether. The quantum benchmark is not used in either functional proof.

papers.title: Products of Trees, $Σ$-theory, Higher Baumslag-Solitar Groups
papers.abstract: We study the $Σ$-theory of groups equipped with multiple HNN decompositions in the case where the product of the associated Bass-Serre trees satisfies the hypotheses of Brown's criterion. We then obtain an explicit description of the $Σ$-theory restricted to the span of all characters dual to one of the HNN decompositions. One consequence is that Meinert's Direct Product Formula holds in this context. As a key ingredient for the proof, we present a purely topological result that allows reading off the essential connectedness and acyclicity properties of products of regular trees with height functions. As the main application of our theorem, we introduce higher Baumslag-Solitar groups. We prove that they admit a canonical system of HNN decompositions, and use it to deduce multiple results, such as the existence of normal forms, and a well-behaved structure of standard parabolic subgroups (which include the vertex and edge groups). By understanding their interplay with a special class of endomorphisms called multiplication maps (which include the structure maps), we control the action on the product of Bass-Serre trees. This allows us to compute the full $Σ$-theory of higher Baumslag-Solitar groups.
papers.comments: 52 pages, 7 figures, no generative AI, comments welcome

papers.title: Another step towards spectral descriptions of cyclic functions
papers.abstract: We consider the operator $V_f=M^{*}_{f}M_{f}$ in the weighted Hardy spaces $H^{2}_ω$, with $M_f$ the operator of multiplication by the function $f$. We determine some basic properties like the essential spectrum when $f$ is a polynomial. Then we focus on the point spectrum when $f$ is a degree 2 polynomial and $H^{2}_ω$ is the Bergman space, assuming that certain parameter is real. We show how this bifurcates into two possibilities: in one we establish the lack of eigenvalues while, in the other, the lack of maximal dimension eigenspaces.

papers.title: Local well-posedness for the Novikov-Veselov equation at subcritical regularity
papers.abstract: We establish local well-posedness of the Novikov--Veselov equation (NV), at every fixed value of the energy parameter, for initial data in $H^s(\mathbb{R}^2)$ in the entire subcritical Sobolev range $s>-1$. The argument is perturbative and does not invoke the integrable structure, instead adapting the strategy in our previous work on KdV (2026). An infinite normal-form expansion indexed by binary trees is combined with a gauge transform that bypasses the obstructions in the associate bilinear estimate, and the resulting gauged equation -- carrying nonlinear contributions of every order -- is closed by a contraction in a Fourier restriction space. The analytic engine is a family of frequency-restricted multilinear bounds, supported by a detailed description of the two-dimensional resonance geometry attached to (NV).

papers.title: Twisted Fourier-Mukai partners of genus 1 curves
papers.abstract: We study twisted derived equivalence between genus 1 curves over an arbitrarly perfect field.

papers.title: Dualizing involutions on Kazhdan-Patterson covers of $\mathrm{GL}(r)$
papers.abstract: Let $F$ be a non-Archimedean local field of characteristic zero and $G=\mathrm{GL}(r,F).$ Let $r,n \geq 2$ and $\widetilde{G}$ be an $n$-fold Kazhdan-Patterson cover of $G$. Let $π$ be an irreducible smooth representation of $G$ and $π^{\vee}$ be the contragredient of $π$. Let $τ$ be an involutive anti-automorphism of $G$ satisfying $π^τ\simeq π^{\vee}$. In this case, we say that $τ$ is a dualizing or duality involution. When $r=2$, it is known that any lift of the standard involution on $G$ to $\widetilde{G}$ is a dualizing involution if and only if $n=2$. In this paper, we study the dualizing property of the lifts of the standard involution on $G$ to $\widetilde{G}$ and prove the following: (i) When $r \geq 2$ and $n \geq 3$, we show that any lift of the standard involution to $\widetilde{G}$ is never a dualizing involution. (ii) When $r=2t$ and $n=2$, we show that any lift of the standard involution to $\widetilde{G}$ is a dualizing involution. (iii) When $r=2t+1$ and $n=2$, we show that there is a unique lift of the standard involution to $\widetilde{G}$ which is a dualizing involution.

papers.title: Stochastic Nonlocal Conservation Laws with Lévy Noise: Stability, BV Estimates, and Vanishing Viscosity
papers.abstract: We study one-dimensional stochastic nonlocal conservation laws with a convolution-type interaction field, driven by multiplicative Brownian noise and compensated Poisson random measures. The nonlocal operator modifies the classical entropy structure, while the jump noise produces nonlinear correction terms in the entropy inequality. We introduce a notion of stochastic entropy solution and establish an $L^1$-stability estimate using spatial doubling of variables and the Itô--Lévy formula. This yields uniqueness in the vanishing-viscosity class and, under additional bounds, a localized Cauchy estimate of order $\sqrt{\varepsilon+\varepsilon'}$. Existence is obtained by vanishing viscosity: we construct the viscous solutions through a Faedo--Galerkin scheme and derive viscosity-uniform $L^1$ and localized $BV$ estimates, which allow us to pass to the limit and obtain a spatially $BV$ stochastic entropy solution.

papers.title: Perfect Matching Complexes of $3\times 2n$ Grid Graph
papers.abstract: The perfect matching complex of a simple graph $G$ is an abstract simplicial complex whose facets (maximal faces) are precisely the perfect matchings of $G$. In this article, we study the topology of the perfect matching complex of the $3\times 2n$ grid graph and show that it is homotopy equivalent to a wedge of $f_{n-1}$ copies of $(n-1)$-dimensional spheres, where $f_{k}$ denotes the $k$-th Fibonacci number. This proves a particular case of the conjecture given by Chandrakar and Singh for perfect matching complex of grid graphs.

papers.title: Compatible zero-sum partitions of finite Abelian groups and their applications
papers.abstract: Let $(Γ,+)$ be a finite Abelian group and let $g\inΓ\setminus\{0\}$. A partition of $Γ$ is called $g$-compatible if no part contains both $x$ and $x+g$. For a prescribed involution $h$ and odd $r\ge3$, we prove that $Γ$ admits an $h$-compatible partition into zero-sum $r$-element sets if and only if $r$ divides $|Γ|$ and $Γ$ has at least three involutions. Moreover, the partition can be chosen so that the multigraph whose vertices are its parts and whose edges are the pairs $\{x,x+h\}$ is Hamiltonian and has a proper edge coloring with $r$ colors. We also give examples, for groups of odd order and for even block sizes, in which zero-sum partitions exist but compatible ones do not. We give two applications of these partitions. For block size three, we obtain complete mappings whose cycles are precisely the parts of the partition. We also construct Hamiltonian $r$-regular $Γ$-distance-magic graphs admitting $0$ and every involution of $Γ$ as magic constants.

papers.title: Strong endpoint estimates for bilinear spherical averaging operators on closed hypersurfaces and curved patches
papers.abstract: Tainara Borges~\cite[Section~7.1, Question~7.2]{Borges2026} asked whether the strong $L^1\times L^1\to L^{1/2}$ estimate for bilinear spherical averages extends to all compact smooth hypersurfaces without boundary and with nonvanishing Gaussian curvature. We give a positive answer when $d\ge2$. The geometric argument concerns the difference projection $(y,z)\mapsto y-z$: at every critical point, two definite directions in its fiber already ensure that the projected surface measure has bounded density. This condition holds for the closed hypersurfaces in the original question. The ensuing strong endpoint uses the localization principle of Iosevich, Palsson and Sovine~\cite[Propositions~4.1--4.2]{IPS2022}. Our proof also establishes a partial positive result for the curvature-rank problem in Borges~\cite[Question~7.1]{Borges2026}. We exhibit a smooth full-curvature patch with boundary for which the strong estimate fails. The endpoint yields the entire fixed-scale Hölder family.

papers.title: A Realizability-Based Kinetic-Fluid Domain Decomposition Method for Single-Temperature Gas Mixtures
papers.abstract: This paper introduces a domain-adaptive numerical method for multi-species kinetic models that relax toward a single-temperature and single-velocity hydrodynamic limit. To this end, we derive moment realizability matrices for this regime. In this way the ideas of Levermore, Morokoff, and Nadiga are extended to non-equilibrium mixtures in which inter-species and intra-species collisions occur at comparable rates, so that all species relax to a common velocity and a common temperature. The realizability conditions are used as an indicator to divide the computational domain, at each time step, into macroscopic and kinetic regions. In the kinetic regions, where the continuum description fails (e.g., across strong shocks, non-equilibrium interfaces, or kinetic boundary layers), the method solves the multi-species kinetic equations. Close to local thermodynamic equilibrium, the Euler equations of the mixture are solved instead. Confining the kinetic computations to the non-equilibrium regions reduces the simulation time, while the results remain close to those of the full kinetic solver. The method is discretized on Cartesian grids with high-order schemes in space and time. The kinetic equations are integrated with an Asymptotic-Preserving Implicit-Explicit (IMEX) scheme, so that a consistent discretization of the single-velocity, single-temperature Euler system of the mixture is recovered when the Knudsen number goes to zero. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first realizability-based adaptive spatial domain decomposition method for gas mixtures in this single-velocity, single-temperature setting.

papers.title: Stochastic inverse source problem in inhomogeneous media: far-field statistics
papers.abstract: This paper is concerned with an inverse random source problem for the stochastic Helmholtz equation in a known three-dimensional inhomogeneous medium. The source is driven by spatial white noise. We seek to recover its mean and strength from the mean and cross-frequency covariance of the far-field pattern. For a smooth nontrapping wave speed, we use the spectral measure of the acoustic operator to relate the far-field data to the source statistics.
