We prove that the singular equation has a unique global strong solution for every initial state in the closed Weyl chamber, including states with coinciding particles. The solutions have locally integrable interaction terms and spend zero Lebesgue time at pairwise collisions. We also consider the equation in which the interaction terms are set to zero at collisions. At certain integer values of $δ$, this equation admits infinitely many solution laws from suitable initial configurations. In these solutions, a block of particles can remain at zero for any prescribed time before being released. For positive initial states, we determine when zero is reached and when particles enter the negative half-line. From distinct initial positions, collisions occur almost surely for $0<κ<1$ and do not occur for $κ\ge1$. Collisions of three or more particles are excluded away from zero. We give an example of a triple collision at zero. We obtain two-sided bounds for the tails of the first-zero and first-collision times. The bounds give matching powers for the first-zero time when it is finite, and for the first-collision time in nonnegative systems when $0<κ<1$.

papers.title: The Moduli of Canonical Threefolds of Minimum Volume
papers.abstract: We determine the moduli space of complex projective canonical threefolds of volume $1/420$. It consists of an irreducible rational component of dimension $33$ and two isolated points, represented by the explicitly constructed rigid threefolds Vega and Altair.
papers.comments: 322 pages. Computational code and data included as ancillary files. Comments are welcome

papers.title: Quadratic APN Functions of $\mathbb{F}_2^{10}$ with a Self-Equivalence of Prime Order
papers.abstract: Almost perfect nonlinear (APN) functions of $\mathbb{F}_2^n$ have the lowest possible differential uniformity. The only known APN permutation in even dimension, in dimension six, is equivalent to a quadratic APN function with a nontrivial linear self-equivalence; no APN permutation is known for even $n \geq 8$. In a published collection of about 3.8 million quadratic APN classes of dimension eight, at most 0.34% have a nontrivial linear self-equivalence. In dimension ten, the 25 literature classes considered here all have one. We study all quadratic APN functions of $\mathbb{F}_2^{10}$ with such a self-equivalence, which usually confines them to a much smaller linear space. Up to conjugacy and power similarity, self-equivalences of prime order have 299 types. We settle 298 of them. Elementary lemmas exclude 280 types, and exhaustive searches confirm this for 242 of them. The other 18 types are settled by exhaustive searches with exact equivalence certificates. Up to extended affine equivalence, the 298 types contain 29 classes of quadratic APN functions, four of them new. This also classifies the quadratic APN functions with coefficients in a subfield. Exactly 24 classes contain one with coefficients in $\mathbb{F}_4$, and all 3 that contain one with coefficients in $\mathbb{F}_{32}$ are among them. The open type consists of the quadratic canonical triplicate functions. They correspond to maximum additive Hermitian rank-distance codes. Three different searches find only the invariants of 16 classes, all among the 29. We conjecture there are no others. No quadratic APN function in the 298 settled types is Carlet-Charpin-Zinoviev equivalent to a permutation.

papers.title: The roads taken in the directed landscape
papers.abstract: Every finite-length path in the directed landscape spends almost all of its time on geodesics. More precisely, let G be the union of the interiors of all geodesics. We prove that, almost surely, every path of finite landscape length lies in G outside a set of times of Hausdorff dimension at most 57/61. We also construct finite-length paths whose exceptional set has dimension at least 1/3. The proof combines quantitative bounds on nearly optimal detours, stochastic domination of the environment outside a geodesic, and a three-geodesic disjointness estimate.

papers.title: Normalized ground state solutions to the nonlinear Born--Infeld problem
papers.abstract: We study normalized solutions to the Born--Infeld problem \begin{equation*} -{\rm div}\left(\frac{\nabla u}{\sqrt{1-|\nabla u|^2}}\right)+μu=f(u)\ \hbox{ in }\mathbb{R}^N,\qquad \int_{\mathbb{R}^N}|u|^2\,dx=2m^2, \end{equation*} $N\ge3$, where $m>0$ is prescribed and $μ>0$ is an unknown Lagrange multiplier. The nonlinearity $f$ is assumed to be superlinear at infinity, with no upper restriction on its growth, and to behave like $|s|^{p-2}s$ near zero, with $2<p<2^*$. Following a Lagrangian approach, we relate the action ground state level $a(μ)$ of the prescribed frequency problem to the masses of its ground states by means of one-sided derivative formulas, which lead to the existence of normalized solutions. A distinctive feature of the Born--Infeld operator is that the gradient constraint makes the energy bounded from below on every mass sphere, even in the $L^2$-supercritical case. For $2+4/N\le p<2^*$ we obtain a threshold $c_*>0$ such that normalized action ground states exist for $m^2>c_*$, and none exist for $m^2<c_*$. In the $L^2$-subcritical case they exist for every $m^2>0$. We prove that every action ground state has constant sign and is radial up to a translation.

papers.title: The BCC Lattice Maximizes the First Positive Neumann Eigenvalue among 3D Lattice Voronoi Cells
papers.abstract: It is shown that, among three-dimensional lattices of fixed covolume, the body-centered cubic lattice maximizes the first positive Neumann eigenvalue of its Voronoi cell uniquely, up to orthogonal transformations.

papers.title: The $\operatorname{Proj}$ construction for pro-graded Huber pairs
papers.abstract: Inspired by the theory of pro-graded adic rings developed recently by Ishizuka and Yoshikawa, we introduce and study the notions of a pro-graded Huber ring and a pro-graded Huber pair \begin{equation*}((\mathcal{A}, \mathcal{A}_{\textrm{gr}}), \mathcal{A}^{+}),\end{equation*}which capture the intuition of a complete Huber ring (or Huber pair) equipped with a dense graded subring. Using these notions, we define and study an analog \begin{equation*}\operatorname{Proj}(\mathcal{A}, \mathcal{A}_{\textrm{gr}}, \mathcal{A}^{+})\end{equation*}of the $\operatorname{Proj}$ construction from algebraic geometry in the realm of adic spaces, without restricting our attention to adic spaces satisfying any Noetherian or finite-type assumptions. We consider gradings both by $\mathbb{Z}$ and by $\mathbb{Z}[1/p]$ for a fixed prime number $p$, so our $\operatorname{Proj}$ construction recovers both classical examples such as usual adic projective space $\mathbb{P}_{K}^{n,\textrm{ad}}$ and infinite-type, perfectoid examples such as perfectoid projective space $\mathbb{P}_{K}^{n,\textrm{perfd}}$. Using GAGA, we prove that the adic analytification of any projective variety $X$ over a nonarchimedean field $K$ can be described as the adic $\operatorname{Proj}$ of a suitable pro-graded affinoid algebra $\mathcal{A}$. Moreover, we prove that in this case $\dim X=\dim \mathcal{A}-1$. We also relate our adic $\operatorname{Proj}$ construction to formal models.

papers.title: Convergence rate of observables in the Marcus-Lushnikov process toward Smoluchowski with singular homogeneous kernels
papers.abstract: We study the approximation of the Smoluchowski coagulation equation by the Marcus--Lushnikov process with $N$ initial particles for the singular family of kernels $K\_α(x,y)=x^{-α}+y^{-α}, α> 0$. For regular mean-field particle systems, pathwise fluctuations are naturally expected on the scale $N^{-1/2}$, whereas sufficiently smooth observables may exhibit a weak error of order $N^{-1}$ after averaging. The singularity of $K\_α$ at the origin makes it unclear whether this second-order mechanism survives. We prove that it does: for a class of sufficiently regular nonlinear functionals of the empirical measure, we establish a weak error of order $N^{-1}$ on finite time intervals. The main mechanism is a regularization produced by the singular dynamics itself. Small clusters coagulate at increasingly large rates, which generates exponential moments in the singular variable $x^{-α}$ and yields a rapid escape from the singularity at zero. We exploit this phenomenon through a Wasserstein-type distance adapted to $x^{-α}$, together with weighted total variation estimates used to construct and control the derivative of the Smoluchowski flow.

papers.title: Fourier Harmonics and Pentagonal Rigidity in the Planar Ulam Floating Body Problem
papers.abstract: We give a new proof that the disk is the only strictly convex planar body floating in equilibrium in every orientation at perimetral densities $σ=1/5$ and $σ=2/5$. The proof uses the Fourier harmonics of the chord-angle function and the closure relations of the associated pentagonal carousel. Their combination gives inequalities that force the body to be a disk.

papers.title: Self-Interpretations and Krají{č}ek-Theories
papers.abstract: We study self-interpretations of theories and their connection to Krajíček-theories. Our two main results are the following. Firstly, if the self-interpretations of a theory form a group in the category ${\sf INT}_3$ of theories and interpretations, then the theory is a Krajíček-theory. Secondly, a sequential theory is a Krajíček-theory iff all its self-interpretations are initial. Here initiality of the interpretation $K$ means roughly that its internal interpretations of the weak theory ${\sf S}^1_2$ are initial in all interpretations of ${\sf S}^1_2$.

papers.title: From Diagonal Coloring to Proper Vertex Labelings Distinguishing Adjacent Facial Sums
papers.abstract: In this paper we study proper vertex labelings of 3-connected plane graphs that give distinct boundary-vertex sums to faces sharing an edge. Let $λ(G)$ be the least $k$ for which labels from $\{0,\ldots,k\}$ suffice, and let $\laml(G)$ be its arbitrary-real-list counterpart. Our two main results are an eight-element list theorem for fullerenes and the universal bound $λ(G)\le708587$ for all 3-connected plane graphs. We establish structural nine- and eight-color bounds, classify triangulations whose vertices of degree at least five form an independent set, and determine their exact diagonal chromatic numbers. We also prove closure under triangular sums for $q\ge7$ diagonal colors, with an optimal uniform threshold. For cubic 3-connected plane graphs we obtain $λ\le14$, improving to $λ\le9$ in the bipartite case.

papers.title: Stability Certification for Approximate Nonlinear Model Predictive Control
papers.abstract: Neural-network approximations of nonlinear model predictive control can reduce online computational costs, but ensuring constraint satisfaction and closed-loop stability remains challenging. We propose a framework in which convex optimisation is used to restore feasibility under suitable local assumptions, while bounds on the corrected controller's cost suboptimality provide sufficient conditions for practical closed-loop stability. To assess these conditions over a compact set of initial states, we investigate a branch-and-bound approach based on convex relaxations of the nonlinear dynamics, with probabilistic guarantees established through scenario optimisation. The proposed approach represents a step towards combining the computational efficiency of approximate nonlinear model predictive control with systematic methods for restoring feasibility and assessing stability.

papers.title: Strongly Monotone Central Path Equations for Quadratic Cone Programs
papers.abstract: We introduce a canonical central path for the homogeneous embedding of quadratic cone programs, defined by strongly monotone equations whose modulus is the barrier parameter. We prove that the path exists uniquely, is smooth, and lies on a sphere of fixed radius. Under mild regularity assumptions, its limit points recover optimal solutions or certificates of infeasibility. Exploiting the fact that the embedding operator has a closed-form resolvent, we derive Josephy-Newton steps that retain the nonlinear embedding equations and linearize only the complementarity conditions. Each step reduces to quasi-definite linear system solves and a scalar quadratic. Using this, we derive a new predictor-corrector interior-point method with a surrogate formulation that allows the predictor and corrector to share a single sparse factorization. We provide an open-source implementation, cpo3, for linear and quadratic programs. On 675 instances from eight benchmark collections, with presolve and crossover disabled, cpo3 achieves the highest verified solve count (631) and the lowest penalized shifted geometric mean runtime among the tested open-source and commercial solvers. It is the only tested solver to solve all 138 Maros-Meszaros instances to high accuracy. Moreover, we establish Euclidean and local-norm error bounds that motivate a warm-start heuristic for the proposed algorithm, yielding up to 2.3x median runtime speedup over cold starts on perturbed Netlib and Maros-Meszaros problems.

papers.title: The random KKM mapping principle and its applications
papers.abstract: Based on the recently developed random Brouwer fixed point theorem and the theory of stable compactness, we establish a random Knaster--Kuratowski--Mazurkiewicz (KKM) mapping principle in Hausdorff topological $L^0$-modules. As consequences of this principle, we obtain several results on fixed points, minimax problems, variational inequalities, and conditional games. These results solve a large class of noncompact problems in random functional analysis and its applications.

papers.title: Stability of crystalline measures under random perturbations
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study random perturbations and the diffraction properties of translation-bounded crystalline measures. Under a non-vanishing assumption on the known perturbation factor, we prove that, almost surely, any realization of the perturbed measure preserves sufficient structural information to allow the full recovery of the original measure. Previous works have only considered crystalline measures with uniformly discrete supports and equal-mass atoms. Our general setting includes many important crystalline measures that were excluded until now. To treat this broader setting, we adopt a different framework. In this work, we model the perturbation as a random measure rather than as a random set. In particular, this leads us to consider not only perturbations of the support, but also perturbations of the atoms' masses. On the other hand, using elementary techniques of Fourier analysis, we prove that any translation-bounded crystalline measure has a diffraction measure, and we explicitly compute its diffraction.
papers.comments: 39 pages; accepted for publication in Transactions of the American Mathematical Society

papers.title: Dynamic Assortment Optimization Under Arbitrary Demand Distributions: The Uniform Price Setting
papers.abstract: We study the joint optimization of assortment and inventory when products are identically priced and the total demand (number of customers) is uncertain. A seller chooses initial inventories before customers arrive and every customer buys her preferred product among those still in stock according to a choice model known to the seller. The objective is to maximize the (expected) total sales, subject to a capacity constraint. We give a $(1-1/e)^2$-approximation under any ranking-based choice model and a $(1-1/e-\varepsilon)$-approximation under the Markov chain choice model, where $\varepsilon$ is a tunable parameter that trades off runtime with approximation guarantee. Our guarantees hold for arbitrary demand distributions and do not require the ubiquitous Increasing Failure Rate (IFR) assumption. In fact, our results also improve on the state-of-the-art approximations for IFR demand distributions. Key to our results is the discovery of hidden submodularity in these problems and the development of efficient procedures to evaluate (or approximate) the objective values. Specifically, we uncover a novel connection to online bipartite matching (for ranking-based models) and use stochastic coupling arguments (for the Markov chain choice model) to reduce the problems to instances of constrained submodular maximization. This opens the door to applying the vast algorithmic machinery for submodular maximization to our problem setting, leading, for example, to natural generalizations beyond cardinality constraint where no approximation results were previously known.

papers.title: Balancing-based model reduction for output-constrained optimal control of switched linear systems
papers.abstract: We develop a balanced-truncation (BT) framework for model-order reduction of optimal control problems governed by switched linear systems, with quadratic tracking costs, convex input constraints, and Moreau--Yosida-regularized output constraints. For general Petrov--Galerkin reduced models, we derive an a posteriori bound for the error in the optimal value function, and combine it with BT-based estimates of the dynamical-system reduction error. We show that BT preserves the duality structure underlying the first-order optimality conditions, making first-reduce-then-optimize and first-optimize-then-reduce equivalent. Consequently, reducing the forward system also reduces the associated optimality system, leading to a certified, online-efficient, and online-adaptive approximation of the parameterized solution operator. The reduced model can therefore be reused across different regularization parameters, constraint sets, switching signals, and reference trajectories.

papers.title: Thresholds of the Polya Szego inequality for the fractional logarithmic p-Laplacian
papers.abstract: We establish three surprising features of the Polya Szego principle for the full signed energy of the fractional logarithmic p-Laplacian. First, the energy doesn't not decrease under rearrangement for all admissible functions. Second, the sharp threshold for Polarization and Schwarz rearrangements are different. Third, for Steiner rearrangement, the threshold in 1 dimension and N dimensions is not the same. Additionally the dimension doesn't appear in the formula.

papers.title: A quotient formula for the Behrend function
papers.abstract: The Behrend function is essential in enumerative geometry. However, computing it, even in zero dimension, has been a highly subtle and mysterious matter since its introduction in the 2000s. We present a quotient formula for the Behrend function of any closed $r$-dimensional affine scheme $X^r \subset \mathbb{A}^N$, evaluated at a singular point, where $0\leq r \leq N-1$. In particular, if the scheme is monomial, we associate parallelepipeds to it and interpret the Behrend function as simple volume information about them. The results here, in particular, recover the recent results of Graffeo-Ricolfi for the zero-dimensional case in 2D in \cite{Graffeo-Ricolfi}, and also the more recent result of Polini-Sammartan-Ulrich on the zero-dimensional case in \cite{PSU26}.

papers.title: Maxwell's equations with thin wires in critical scaling
papers.abstract: We derive effective equations for a situation in which electromagnetic waves hit an array of very thin wires. We study two cases, perfectly conducting wires and highly conducting wires, and investigate in both the critical scaling of the parameters. The electric field $E^η$ and the magnetic field $H^η$ satisfy the time-harmonic Maxwell equations, and the small parameter $η>0$ is the spacing of the wires. A non-critical scaling of the wires implies either that the wires have no effect or that the tangential component of the limiting electric field in the direction of the wires vanishes along the effective interface. In the critical scaling, we observe an interesting effect: The wires act as oscillators and there is a relation between the electric field in longitudinal direction and the jump of the magnetic field in transversal direction involving second derivatives of a flux quantity.

papers.title: An Obstruction to Realizing Aspherical $3$-Manifold Groups via Torus Surgery
papers.abstract: Let $Y$ be a closed, connected, oriented, aspherical $3$-manifold with fundamental group $π= π_1(Y)$ and positive first Betti number $β_1(Y) > 0$, and let $X_0 = Y \times S^1$. We prove that no torus surgery on $X_0$ along a torus-fibered $T^2$-knot $T \subseteq X_0$ can yield a $4$-manifold $X = X_{0; T, f}$ with fundamental group $π$. The obstruction combines the vanishing of the Euler characteristic of $X$ with a classifying-map argument showing that the unimodular intersection form on $H^2(X; \mathbb{Z})$ must admit an isotropic subgroup of rank $β_1(π)$, forcing $χ(X) \geq 2$. Along the way, we also present an independent geometric proof via covering space theory, the Sphere Theorem, and Scott's Core Theorem that the fundamental group of a closed aspherical $3$-manifold is torsion-free.

papers.title: On four problems from the Kourovka Notebook: spectra, periodic automorphism groups, commutators, and operator simplicity
papers.abstract: We examine Problems 18.62(a), 18.63, 18.65, and 20.120 of the Kourovka Notebook. First, a family of semidirect products involving $\operatorname{PSL}_2(p^2)$ gives arbitrarily many pairwise nonisomorphic groups critical with respect to one simple-group spectrum, subject to explicit arithmetic congruences. Second, a completed-algebra construction using sparse torsion identities and a matrix Golod-Shafarevich-Vinberg inequality produces an infinite periodic group generated by two fixed-point-free automorphisms of order five of an abelian group. Third, we give a short matrix proof that the class of elements of order three in $\operatorname{PSL}_2(8)$ contradicts the assertion in Problem 18.65 as written. Finally, we spell out how P. Hall's 1962 wreath-power theorems answer Problem 20.120 under the usual normal-subgroup meaning of simplicity for a group with one distinguished automorphism. The four arguments have substantially different provenance. In particular, the last is a consequence of a known construction, not a priority claim. The two longer constructions are recorded in detail for independent mathematical scrutiny.

papers.title: Score-based neural ordinary differential equations for reaction-diffusions
papers.abstract: A diffusion equation can be rewritten as a transport equation driven by the score function of the evolving density. Conventional probability-flow formulations, which move particles deterministically with this score-driven velocity, typically conserve total mass. In this work, we develop a Lagrangian method for reaction-diffusion equations in which each particle carries a position and a physical weight. The characteristic ODEs incorporate source terms into the evolution of the log-density and its gradient, while particle weights track changes in mass. We combine this representation with a learned velocity field and weighted particle training to approximate these dynamics. For non-increasing reaction rates, a relative-entropy inequality supports the mass-normalized self-consistency residual as the training objective. This objective can control the error of the induced density when the growth rate is bounded. The algorithm divides the time interval into short windows. In each window, a frozen velocity generates the particle data for a regression of the network velocity. We draw the particles from period-adapted initial sampling distributions and weight them in the loss partly by their predicted future mass, because the reaction can make regions with little initial mass important later. We numerically investigate the method on the Ornstein--Uhlenbeck (OU) equation with a linear source term, Fisher--KPP equations, and Wasserstein--Fisher--Rao gradient flows.

papers.title: Efficient Reconfiguration of Independent Transversals
papers.abstract: We study the reconfiguration of independent transversals in graphs with a prescribed vertex partition. Given a graph $G$ with a vertex partition $\mathcal{V}=(V_1,\ldots,V_m)$, an independent transversal is an independent set containing exactly one vertex from each part $V_i$ of $\mathcal{V}$. The reconfiguration problem concerns transforming one independent transversal into another through a sequence of local changes, while preserving the independent transversal property at every step. For any fixed $r\in\mathbb{N}$ and $ε>0$, we present a polynomial-time algorithm that, given an $r$-claw-free graph $G$ with a vertex partition $\mathcal{V}=(V_1,\ldots,V_m)$ and two independent transversals $S$ and $R$, either finds a polynomial-length reconfiguration path between $S$ and $R$, or identifies a nonempty set of partition classes $\mathcal{B}\subseteq\mathcal{V}$ such that the subgraph induced by their union admits a strong dominating set of size at most $(2+ε)|\mathcal{B}|$. Our result provides an algorithmic counterpart to recent connectivity results for the reconfiguration graph of all independent transversals, and establishes polynomial bounds on its diameter under suitable conditions. As a specific application, we obtain a polynomial-time algorithm for reconfiguring perfect matchings in $r$-uniform bipartite hypergraphs $H=(A,B,E)$, that either produces a polynomial-length reconfiguration path between two given perfect matchings or identifies a subset $S\subseteq A$ whose link hypergraph $E_S$ in $B$ has a small cover.

papers.title: Beyond Blossom: Accelerating MWPM Decoding for Surface Codes With Local Predecoding and Architecture-Aware Optimizations
papers.abstract: Minimum-weight perfect matching (MWPM) is widely used to decode surface codes, but its computational cost increases with code distance. We present Beyond Blossom, a state-of-the-art CPU-based MWPM decoder for surface codes. It combines algorithmic optimization through local predecoding, architecture-aware optimization, and pipeline-wide parallelism to reduce matching workload and execution overhead while preserving MWPM optimality. Across rotated surface codes with distances 9-33 and circuit-level physical error rates of 0.05%-0.3%, on a single CPU core, Beyond Blossom achieves a 4.23$\times$ geometric-mean speedup and up to 5.58$\times$ speedup over Sparse Blossom in PyMatching. At distance 33 and a physical error rate of 0.1%, with 8 CPU cores, decoding a block of 33 measurement rounds takes 21.40 $μ$s on average, equivalent to 0.65 $μ$s per round.

papers.title: Rigidity of the moving particle lemma for the interchange process
papers.abstract: Let $G=(V,c)$ be a finite connected weighted graph. We establish the exact conditions for attaining equality in the moving particle lemma for the interchange process on $G$ subject to a unit voltage drop across two terminal vertices $x\neq y \in V$. First, equality can occur only in irreducible representations indexed by partitions with at most two rows. We then show that the equality phenomenon beyond the constant and linear sectors is already visible in the two-particle exclusion process. Such equality occurs in exactly two cases: either the harmonic $x$--$y$ voltage is $\frac12$ on every nonterminal vertex, and the induced nonterminal graph $G[V\setminus\{x,y\}]$ is disconnected; or the harmonic voltage is constant on each connected component of $G[V\setminus \{x,y\}]$, and both voltage values $a$ and $1-a$, with $0\le a<\frac12$, occur. In each case we compute the equality kernel in every degree and particle sector. The resulting decomposition gives the complete equality kernel for exclusion and, through the regular representation, for the interchange process.

papers.title: Multiplicity of Positive Solutions for Singular Anisotropic Elliptic Equations with Variable Exponents
papers.abstract: We study anisotropic elliptic Dirichlet problems with variable exponents, singular nonlinearities, and subcritical superlinear reactions. Our contribution is a direct variational construction that combines Nehari geometry and fibering maps without requiring global differentiability of the singular energy, and the result establishes the existence of two positive weak solutions for sufficiently small \(λ\), distinguished by their energy signs.

papers.title: Cohen Macaulayness and Buchsbaumness of Cartesian Products of Paths and Cycles
papers.abstract: We study the independence complexes of Cartesian products of paths and cycles. Let G(m,n) denote the Cartesian product of the path P_m and the cycle C_n, and let Delta(m,n) denote its independence complex. We determine the well-covered graphs in this family and use reduced homology to study their Cohen-Macaulay and Buchsbaum properties. Using these results, we completely classify the Cohen-Macaulay members. We then study the Buchsbaum property of Delta(m,n) through vertex links. For the remaining family P_m x C_3, we introduce an auxiliary family of graphs and use an inductive link argument together with Reisner's criterion to determine precisely when the independence complex of P_m x C_3 is Buchsbaum. Combining this with the remaining well-covered cases yields the complete Buchsbaum classification.

papers.title: On a generalization of result due to Peskine and Szpiro-II
papers.abstract: Let $(R,\mathfrak{m})$ be a regular local ring and let $I$ be a Cohen-Macaulay ideal of $R$. When $\operatorname{Char} R=p>0$, a result of Peskine and Szpiro proves that $H^i_I(R)=0$ for $i\neq\operatorname{height} I$. This result is not true when $\operatorname{Char} R=0$. In this article, we prove that the Bass numbers of $H^{\operatorname{height} I}_I(R)$ completely determines the vanishing of $H^i_I(R)$ for $i\neq \operatorname{height} I$. This result was previously established by the second author in the equicharacteristic case and more generally for Gorenstein local rings by Hellus and Schenzel. In contrast to the spectral sequence methods employed by Hellus and Schenzel, our proof is elementary and self-contained.

papers.title: Restoring Consistency with Poynting's Theorem in Numerical MHD and RMHD
papers.abstract: For perfectly conducting plasmas, Poynting's theorem states that the time rate of change of electromagnetic energy density equals the negative of the divergence of the Poynting flux. To the best of our knowledge, this involutive theorem has never been mimetically incorporated in codes. We show that there is an inconsistency in MHD and RMHD codes that evolve face-centered magnetic fields in globally-divergence-free fashion. This is because the face-centered flux of energy density, which incorporates a Poynting vector, is evaluated using one-dimensional Riemann solvers that are applied at face-centers. However, the face-centered magnetic fields are evolved according to edge-centered electric fields that come from two-dimensional Riemann solvers that are applied to the edges of a zone. While edge-centered electric fields are used to evolve the magnetic field, they have no influence on the face-centered Poynting flux. For situations where the magnetic energy is much larger than the thermal energy, this causes a negative pressure to be evaluated at the zone-centers. This paper restores consistency by using edge-centered variables to evaluate a face-centered Poynting flux. A simple accuracy-preserving correction is made to the face-centered flux of energy density. We show that it helps considerably in simulations that have very strong magnetic fields.

papers.title: Polytopal realization of double root free subword complexes
papers.abstract: We give a convex geometric sufficient condition for a convex polytope to realize a spherical subword complex. Using this criterion, we first prove that each root independent spherical subword complex is polytopal, for any Coxeter group. Then we prove the polytopality of double root free subword complexes, for any Coxeter groups. To prove this, we construct a polytope in an auxiliary vector space whose image under a natural affine map is the usual brick polytope. In the complex Kac-Moody case, the polytope is integral, with vertices in the character lattice of the torus of unfolded galleries in a thick building. In finite Lie types, in double root free cases, these tori are precisely the corresponding braid varieties.

papers.title: On Zhao's conjectural basis for finite multiple zeta values
papers.abstract: We prove a conjecture by J. Zhao which states that every finite multiple zeta value associated with a nonempty index is a $\mathbb{Q}$-linear combination of $ζ^{}_{\mathcal{A}}(k_1,\dots, k_r, 2, 1)$, where $k_i\in \{2, 3\}$. Our proof proceeds by constructing a basis for the space of formal multiple zeta values defined by the confluence relations. This approach also reduces the Kaneko--Zagier conjecture (apart from compatibility with the depth filtration) to linear independence conjectures for ordinary and finite multiple zeta values, without using motivic theory.

papers.title: Valid Inequalities for Bilevel 0-1 Shortest-Path Problems
papers.abstract: We characterize valid inequalities for bilevel programs in which the leader makes binary decisions, and the follower solves a shortest-path problem. We exploit a dualize-and-combine reformulation and show that even with ideal formulations for the leader and the follower primal solution sets, fractional solutions may still appear in the continuous relaxation. From that reformulation, we identify that the interaction between the leader variables and the follower dual variables, which we capture through a leader-potential set, is the key structure to be convexified to guarantee that a continuous relaxation recovers the optimal value of the original problem, closing the objective gap. Furthermore, we characterize the valid inequalities for the leader-potential set through network flows, and identify a family of inequalities we name root cuts that suffice to recover the optimal value. Complementary to the structural results, we prove that the cut generation problem is NP-hard even with partially fixed coefficients and a network with two nodes and two parallel arcs. Motivated by the complexity result, we propose a constructive method to fix coefficients in the valid inequalities while preserving separation guarantees, by exploiting the network structure.

papers.title: Why Finite Intelligence Works in an Infinite World: A Mathematical Theory
papers.abstract: An information system often has to learn before it knows what it will be asked. A finite representation can succeed without recording an infinite environment in full when those asks share collective structure, rather than demand unrelated facts scattered arbitrarily across it. We formalize this phenomenon through future-task information, the minimum retained information needed to preserve decision value relative to the available evidence. A joint decision-regret state records posterior comparisons among actions for every permitted task. Under compactness assumptions, every retained representation admits a calibrated replacement based on this state, preserving all task regrets without increasing information; the resulting information-regret curve equals an operational coding rate. Two exact boundaries govern finite preservation: weak-star closure for a fixed action count, and the singular mass of the source-evidence law when all finite action menus are admitted. Collective structure determines information requirements beyond individual-question difficulty. Families with identical source laws, pairwise task metrics, and individual-task rates can have different high-resolution exponents. Covariance-identical coordinate and parity families have different exact rate-distortion curves, with optimal parity retention characterized by a sharp Fourier-entropy inequality. For balanced nested task families, refinement sizes and weighted reach determine the rate within an additive constant, attained by prefix coding under explicit decay conditions. Nonlinear learning and computational separations distinguish preservation from efficient discovery and use. The proposed mathematical theory identifies which shared decision requirements allow finite information to remain useful for infinitely many possible purposes.

papers.title: Internal diameter bounds for DLA on random planar maps under invariance principles
papers.abstract: We establish sublinear bounds for the internal diameter of External Diffusion Limited Aggregation (DLA) clusters on random planar maps. We develop two conditional DLA growth results for deterministic planar maps: the weaker condition yielding sublinear growth for DLA, and the stronger yielding polynomially sublinear growth for DLA. We then verify the strong assumption a.s. for the $γ$-mated CRT maps, and the weak condition a.s. for ergodic scale-free random environments, establishing the corresponding a.s bounds.

papers.title: No free lattice contains an infinite ascending chain of copies of FL(3)
papers.abstract: No free lattice contains an infinite strictly ascending chain of sublattices isomorphic to FL(3), the free lattice on three generators; this answers a question that R. A. Dean asked and the second author's 1997 notes on the problem left open. Every such chain would yield, inside FL(3), a coherent chain of proper self-embeddings $Θ_0, Θ_1, Θ_2, \dots$ with $Θ_k \circ Θ_j = Θ_j$ for $j < k$, so that each later embedding fixes the image of each earlier one pointwise. Every proper self-embedding of FL(3) whose fixed sublattice contains a free generating triple fixes one of the three generators, say $z$, because a power of it or of its dual lies above the identity, and a self-embedding that moves every generator and lies above the identity fixes at most eleven elements. Up to duality, a proper self-embedding fixing the image of such a $Θ_1$ pointwise fixes only elements above $z \wedge (x \vee y)$, where no free generating triple containing $z$ can lie. We also verify the one-step example of the 1997 notes, prove that no step toward such a chain is self-similar, and show that the configuration the argument rules out at length three does occur at length two. Without freeness the answer reverses: FL(3) contains an infinite strictly ascending chain of 3-generated sublattices, so the lattice analogue of Takahasi's chain condition for free groups fails. The theorem itself is checked by the Agda proof assistant under its safe flags, for free lattices over generators with decidable equality, and its formal proof uses no classical principle: finite searches and an induction on a finite set replace the infinite pigeonhole principle by which a chain yields a coherent chain.
papers.comments: 59 pages, 13 figures; the main theorem is checked in Agda; the formal development is available at https://github.com/ualib/agda-deans-problem

papers.title: Polynomial-Time Solvability of the Multi-Dimensional Slope Change Problem
papers.abstract: Slope change detection seeks to identify changes in the trends of time-ordered signals. We study the problem of fitting a multidimensional time series by continuous piecewise-linear functions with a shared continuous breakpoint and unrestricted slopes. We consider both the dense setting, in which every dimension may change slope, and the sparse setting, in which at most $k$ dimensions may change slope. Although the resulting optimization problems are nonconvex mixed integer nonlinear programs and may have irrational optimal solutions even for rational data, we prove that all six variants, corresponding to the $\ell_1$, $\ell_2$, and $\ell_\infty$ losses in both settings, are exactly solvable in polynomial time. For least-squares loss, we obtain efficient algorithms requiring $O(JT)$ operations in the dense setting and $O(J^2T\log J)$ operations in the sparse setting, where $T$ is the number of time points and $J$ is the number of dimensions. We implement these least-squares algorithms and evaluate them on simulated data and three real-world time series, namely, surface temperatures (ERA5), hand-tracking data from a mixed-reality headset (HoloAssist), and turbofan engine sensor data (NASA C-MAPSS). The dense algorithm solves instances with up to $J=10^5$ and $T=100$, that is, $10^7$ observations, in less than $0.1$ seconds on a laptop, while the sparse algorithm solves instances with about $10^3$ dimensions and up to $T=240$ in under a second. Compared with a mixed-integer nonlinear programming (MINLP) formulation solved by Gurobi, our algorithms are several orders of magnitude faster (approximately $8.9 \times 10^3$ to $3.4 \times 10^6$ times) on instances where Gurobi terminates within its default optimality tolerance of $0.01\%$ optimality gap. On larger instances, Gurobi frequently reaches a 10,000-second time limit with substantial optimality gaps.

papers.title: The Klein-Gordon equation in projective geometry
papers.abstract: We discuss a geometric method by which Hörmander's result on the asymptotics of a Klein-Gordon field, on an asymptotically flat spacetime, can be related to some partial peeling, à la Penrose, along an extended projective boundary, embedded in a spacetime with one dimension higher.

papers.title: Sharp nonuniqueness for the Vlasov--Navier--Stokes system
papers.abstract: We consider the Vlasov--Navier--Stokes system on $\mathbb T^d\times\mathbb R^d$, $d\ge2$. For smooth data and every $p<2$, $q<\infty$, we construct infinitely many weak solutions with velocity in $L^p_tL^\infty\cap L^1_tW^{1,q}$ and bounded, renormalized distribution function; infinitely many of them violate the energy inequality. For smooth velocity data, weak solutions with velocity in $L^2_tL^\infty$ are unique, so the result is sharp at the endpoint of the Ladyzhenskaya--Prodi--Serrin scale. The fluid carries the nonuniqueness, through the convex integration scheme of Cheskidov and Luo, and the kinetic equation is solved exactly. The main new difficulty is the memory of the particles: the kinetic state at time $t$ depends on the whole past of the velocity, so a modification on a short interval changes the system at all later times. We overcome it by a causal gluing, carried out from left to right in time, which re-solves the system on every interval of regularity. This yields wild solutions that are strong outside a closed set of times of arbitrarily small Hausdorff dimension. A causal mollification extends the construction to rough data, including every finite-energy velocity datum in dimensions two and three; in two dimensions the energy class is thus exactly the borderline of uniqueness. Finally, in three dimensions we construct Leray solutions satisfying the strong energy inequality and show that they are strong outside a closed set of times of vanishing $\mathcal H^{1/2}$ measure.

papers.title: Towards invertibility of derived categories of sheaf-theoretic line operators
papers.abstract: We investigate when the braided monoidal $\infty$-categories of sheaf-theoretic line operators of $3$-dimensional topological quantum field theories are invertible in the higher Morita category, so that they determine invertible $4$-dimensional anomaly theories. We consider a zoo of different examples which are inherently derived. First, enhancing Ben-Zvi--Francis--Nadler, we show that a symmetric monoidal category of quasi-coherent sheaves $\mathrm{QC}(X)$ is invertible only if $X$ is a point, and convolution categories on loop stacks are Morita trivial whenever the stack satisfies descent along its diagonal, e.g. for classifying stacks. Secondly, we provide an example showing that, unlike for finite braided tensor categories, non-degeneracy does not imply invertibility in the derived setting: For an odd vector space $V[1]$, the $2$-shifted $\mathcal{D}$-modules $\mathrm{DMod}^2(V[1])$ are $3$-dualizable and non-degenerate but neither factorizable nor cofactorizable. This category is closely related to the line operators of linear Rozansky--Witten theory. Finally, we define an anomaly of a group action on an invertible braided monoidal $\infty$-category as a Witt class over $\mathrm{Rep}(G)$, and show that the category of representations of the quantum group of a torus at a root of unity is invertible relative to its quantum Frobenius.

papers.title: On the pure part of the cohomology of character varieties
papers.abstract: We prove the purity conjecture of Hausel and Rodriguez-Villegas relating the graded dimension of the pure part of the cohomology of the twisted character variety $M^B(r,d)$ of $GL(r)$ of genus $g$ with the cohomology of a suitable quiver variety associated to the quiver $S_g$ with one vertex and $g$ loops. In particular, this provides an explicit formula for the pure part of the mixed Hodge polynomial of $M^B(r,d)$ in terms of the Kac polynomial $A_{S_g,r}(q)$. Our approach is based on the $P=W$ theorem to transfer the purity conjecture into a statement about the perverse filtration on the cohomology of th stack of Higgs bundles on a genus $g$ curve. We use the theory of BPS Lie algebras, their $χ$-independence property (proven by Kinjo-Koseki), the recent proof of the stack version of $P=C$ due to Picovschi and Davison's analytic neighborhood theorem to reduce the conjecture to a comparison problem between (the 'pure' part) of the BPS Lie algebra asociated to the stack of Higgs bundles on a genus $g$ curve and the BPS Lie algebra of the stack of representations of the preprojective algebra of the quiver $S_g$. This last step is taken care of by a quiver analog of Markman's tautological generation theorem for the BPS Lie algebra of arbitrary quivers (this last result is also proven by Davison and Hennecart).

papers.title: Equivariant Quantisation of Hypertoric Varieties via Symplectic Cuts
papers.abstract: We study the equivariant geometric quantisation of a non-compact hypertoric orbifold of complex dimension $2n$ by compact symplectic cuts. When the defining arrangement has a non-empty bounded base region and the fixed lift is integral, we prove that, at every positive regular integral level $d$, the space of sections on the cut is the sum of the fibre-rotation weight spaces of weight at most $d$ in the original quantisation. The higher cohomology of the cut pre-quantum line orbibundle vanishes, so its equivariant index is the character of its actual section space. Using the moment polyptychs introduced in a companion paper (arXiv:2610.37724), we give an orbifold Kawasaki-Riemann-Roch localisation formula for this character. We also compute it as a weighted lattice-point sum: a residual weight $x$ occurs at level $d$ if and only if the arrangement slack function satisfies $\mathcal{S}(x) \leq d$, with multiplicity $\binom{d - \mathcal{S}(x) + n}{n}$. The examples compare these calculations in rank one, including a cut with an orbifold point, and in rank two, for smooth cuts that are not toric.
papers.comments: 28 pages, 5 figures. Part II of two; Part I is arXiv:2610.37724. v2: references added, minor corrections

papers.title: Geometric structure of Green currents for holomorphic correspondences on projective surfaces
papers.abstract: Let $f$ be a holomorphic correspondence on a complex projective surface $X$ such that $f^{-1}$ is also holomorphic. Assume that the action of $f^*$ on cohomology is simple and that the dynamical degrees of $f$ satisfy $d_1>\max\{d_0,d_2\}$. We prove that the Green currents $T^\pm$ associated with $f$ are woven. We also provide a large family of examples of holomorphic correspondences satisfying our assumptions, obtained as generic complete intersections in $X\times X$.

papers.title: Many more odd zeta values are irrational
papers.abstract: We prove that for any sufficiently large odd integer $s$, there exist at least \[ 2.78 \, \sqrt{\frac{s \log\log s}{\log s}} \] irrational values among $ζ(3), ζ(5), \dots, ζ(s)$, where $ζ$ is the Riemann zeta function. This improves on the best known estimate by a constant factor times $\sqrt{ \log\log s}$. The proof combines the elimination technique and an arithmetic lemma of Fischler--Sprang--Zudilin, the hypergeometric constructions of Lai--Yu, and the Hankel determinant method that appeared in the proof that $ζ(5)$ is irrational posted by Fauzan on September 17, 2026.

papers.title: Fluctuations of Local Patterns in Non-Periodic Uniquely Ergodic Systems
papers.abstract: We study various families of non-periodic configurations of symbols assigned to vertices of regular graphs. We restrict ourselves to such systems where considered configurations support a uniquely ergodic measure. Symbols can be interpreted as particles and we are concerned with configurations which minimize the interaction energy of particles, the so-called ground-state configurations. One of the main questions then is whether ground-state configurations are stable with respect to small perturbations of interactions. Such stability may be interpreted as a sort of rigidity of non-periodic structures such as tilings, substitution systems, Sturmian systems, and other uniquely ergodic non-periodic systems. We introduce a property of bounded fluctuations of finite patterns of non-periodic configurations, the so-called Strict Boundary Property. We discuss how relevant this property is for stability of non-periodic structures. Examples of Robinson's tilings, Thue-Morse, and Sturmian systems are presented. Some open problems are formulated.
papers.comments: To appear in Perspectives on Ergodic Theory and Its Interactions, In Honor of Vitaly Bergelson, Birkhauser Trends in Mathematics

papers.title: TSP instances that require exponentially many subtour elimination constraints
papers.abstract: We construct pathological TSP instances that require exponentially many subtour elimination constraints (SECs) in the sense that, if a smaller collection of SECs is imposed, then the Dantzig-Fulkerson-Johnson model returns a disconnected solution costing less than an optimal tour. For asymmetric instances on $n$ vertices, we prove a growth rate of \(Ω(φ^n)\), where \(φ\approx 1.618\) is the golden ratio. A node-splitting reduction gives metric instances with \(Ω(φ^{n/2})\) growth. We also give instances in the plane under the Euclidean, Rectilinear, and Maximum metrics that require exponentially many SECs. Concorde struggles on them, with solve times growing exponentially despite tiny integrality gaps.

papers.title: Evolutionary-based Transfer Learning for Physical Attack on End-to-End Autoencoder Communications
papers.abstract: End-to-end autoencoder communication has emerged as a promising means of achieving efficient data transmission across various domains. Nevertheless, vulnerabilities have recently been revealed in these systems by adversarial attacks, wherein malevolent entities manipulate the transmitted signals to deceive the autoencoder. This paper leverages the applications of evolutionary algorithms to solve a challenging optimization problem of launching physical attacks against end-to-end autoencoder communication. For white-box scenarios, we introduce PAGA (Physical Attack based on Genetic Algorithm), which combines a genetic algorithm with elite population initialization to craft attack signals that degrade autoencoder performance. To gauge the efficacy of these attack signals, we employ a fitness function that assesses their capacity to induce substantial reconstruction errors and misclassification rates. A Multi-Factorial version of PAGA, referred to as PAMFGA, is proposed to deal with practical scenarios where the attackers have limited knowledge about the receiver, also known as a black-box attack. Our experimental results show that the proposed attacks can substantially degrade the reliability of the considered autoencoder communication systems across the evaluated settings. This study also underscores the critical importance of incorporating security considerations into the design and implementation of end-to-end autoencoder communication systems.
papers.comments: 31 pages, 10 figures, and 4 tables. Accepted by JNCA

papers.title: Admissibility-Preserving Control for Block Strict-Feedback Systems Under Time-Varying Asymmetric Actuator and State Constraints
papers.abstract: This paper addresses the tracking control of block strict-feedback nonlinear systems subject to time-varying asymmetric actuator and full state constraints. To that end, we develop a time-varying Admissibility-Preserving Control (APC) framework, in which the Admissibility-Preserving Input Realization (APIR) generates the plant input through a dynamic realization. The APIR guarantees input admissibility under the moving actuator set whenever each actuator bound contracts slower than the decay rate of the realization, and a closed-form lower bound on its gain is derived. The state constraints are handled by a logarithmic barrier coordinate at every backstepping step, with widths measured from the virtual control to the moving envelope of the corresponding state. We prove that every state lies inside its envelope, with each virtual control only required to remain inside the envelope of the next state, while the tracking error converges to zero exponentially. Simulations demonstrate the efficacy of the proposed safety-critical control scheme.

papers.title: Graded unitarity constraints on simply-laced affine Kac--Moody algebras
papers.abstract: We investigate constraints imposed by four-dimensional unitarity (recently formalised as graded unitarity) on possible simply-laced affine Kac--Moody vertex algebras arising from four dimensions via the SCFT/VOA correspondence. Under the assumption that the $\mathfrak{R}$-filtration is weight-based with respect to the currents and the Casimir operators, with appropriately shifted $R$-charge assignments for the latter, we demonstrate that all values of the level other than a discrete set are incompatible with four-dimensional unitarity. This set includes all the boundary admissible affine vertex algebras, those corresponding to rank-one Kodaira SCFTs, as well as certain non-admissible families conjecturally associated with specific $D^b_q(\mathfrak{g})$ Argyres--Douglas theories. Specialising to $\mathfrak{sl}_N$ with $N$ prime, we find a stronger result: under the same $\mathfrak{R}$-filtration assumption, four-dimensional unitarity rules out all levels except the boundary admissible $k = k_{N,q}$, which are precisely those corresponding to the $D_q^N(\mathfrak{sl}_N)$ Argyres--Douglas theories.

papers.title: Fast mixing and thermal phases from strong decay of correlations
papers.abstract: We show that a strong form of correlation decay in quantum Gibbs states has far-reaching dynamical consequences. For a smooth path of geometrically local commuting Hamiltonians whose Gibbs states satisfy strong decay of correlations, we construct $\mathrm{O}(1)$-time quasi-local Lindbladian evolutions exactly connecting these states in both directions, together with $\mathrm{O}(1)$-time quasi-local Hamiltonian evolutions exactly connecting their canonical purifications. These quasi-local connections strengthen previously known quantum-channel circuit constructions based on the decay of connected correlation functions [R. Ma, V. Khemani, and S. Sang, PRX Quantum 7, 033052 (2026)], which approximately connect states within the same phase but have depths that grow logarithmically with system size. Furthermore, if the Gibbs-state path contains a product state, we prove that the single-site Glauber dynamics has a $Ω(1)$ spectral gap independent of the system size throughout the path. This establishes Glauber-dynamics fast mixing for models that may violate the strong spatial mixing condition used in prior proofs, including (1) the $q$-state Potts model throughout the high-temperature phase for any $q$ and any finite dimension; (2) the Ising model with a longitudinal field at low temperature, with frustrating perturbations that destroy monotonicity of the dynamics; and (3) the three-dimensional $\mathbb{Z}_2$ lattice gauge theory at low temperatures comparing to a field perturbation, even though the model supports classical memories at intermediate temperatures. Intriguingly, we establish fast mixing of these classical Markov chains using tools from quantum physics like Lieb-Robinson bounds.

papers.title: Methanol substitution suppresses deflagration-excited knock and increases the efficiency of a hydrogen-fuelled CFR engine
papers.abstract: Knock restricts the performance of hydrogen spark-ignition engines and is usually attributed to end-gas autoignition. To the authors' knowledge, this is the first study in which methanol is used to replace part of the hydrogen in a hydrogen engine at constant fuel energy addition, and it shows that near the knock boundary the limiting oscillation is excited by the deflagration itself, which methanol removes without derating the performance. Port-injected methanol replaced 20--50% of the hydrogen energy in a variable-compression Cooperative Fuel Research engine at 600 rpm and compression ratios of 8--12. With pure hydrogen, oscillation in the 4--15 kHz range began before 10% of the charge had burned in 97--100% of cycles, and its maximum amplitude (MAPO) followed the maximum pressure-rise rate across 2499 cycles (Spearman $ρ=0.94$). Methanol slowed the deflagration: it replaced high-flame-speed hydrogen, cooled the intake by 24--25 K and, at unchanged intake pressure, enleaned the mixture by 10--13%. At 50% methanol, the 10--90% combustion duration lengthened 2.7--3.0-fold, oscillation onset moved 4.5--8.3$^\circ$CA after CA10 and mean MAPO fell by 89--93% although the spark timing was advanced by 13--19$^\circ$CA, and IMEP and indicated thermal efficiency rose by 2.4--7.8%. Methanol was thus worth more than this advance, and at matched CA50 MAPO was still about 90% lower. The measured combustion duration of all 25 data sets scaled with the computed laminar flame speed as $S_L^{-0.58}$ ($R^2=0.99$); fuel replacement accounted for about three quarters of the reduction in $S_L$, and the end-gas autoignition integral stayed below 0.07, against 1 at autoignition. The chamber kept its cylindrical acoustic modes, whose frequencies fell by 8--9%. The trade-off is formaldehyde emissions, which rose five- to sixfold while NO$_x$ fell by 49--85%.

papers.title: Classification with Large-Step Gradient Descent: Unifying Self-Stabilization and Convergence Rates
papers.abstract: Neural networks are often trained with gradient descent (GD) using step sizes that exceed classical stability thresholds, a regime where standard convergence theory no longer applies. Despite exhibiting non-monotonic loss and oscillatory dynamics, this regime frequently leads to faster convergence and better generalization. Existing theoretical perspectives offer complementary but incomplete insights: one identifies a self-stabilization mechanism that drives GD toward flat regions but does not yield convergence rates; another derives rigorous rates for specific losses but does not explain the underlying stabilization mechanism; and a third unifies these views for overparameterized least squares, but relies on the existence of a minimizer manifold, which is absent in classification settings. In this work, we extend this unified geometric perspective to exponential-tail losses, including logistic and cross-entropy losses in separable linear classification, where the loss infimum is not attained at any finite parameter. We identify a curvature-defined reference subspace that replaces the role of the minimizer manifold, yielding a coupled dynamical system in which orthogonal oscillations are damped by parallel progress along directions of decreasing sharpness. Under regularity conditions, which we verify for logistic and multiclass cross-entropy losses on symmetric data models, we derive explicit bounds for the iterates, not just the loss, covering both the unstable and stable regimes, and revealing a three-phase damping structure in the latter. Our analysis further uncovers a transient implicit bias induced by large step sizes: although GD converges asymptotically to the max-margin direction, large steps can leave persistent orthogonal residuals and, in certain geometries, amplify them, affecting finite-time alignment with the max-margin direction.

papers.title: SURFACE: Preference Distribution Matching on Pareto Fronts via Scalarization Steering
papers.abstract: Constructing a finite Pareto representation requires allocating a limited number of solutions across the Pareto front (PF). A desired preference distribution specifies this allocation by assigning more solutions to some PF regions and fewer to others. Scalarization generates Pareto solutions by varying objective weights and solving single-objective problems. However, a distribution of scalarization weights generally does not translate into the same distribution of Pareto solutions along the PF, because the weight-to-solution map is nonlinear and unknown in advance.To account for this distortion, we introduce SURFACE (Scalarization Updates for Redistributing Finite Approximations with Chart Estimation}), which adaptively updates scalarization weights to match a desired PF distribution. SURFACE estimates how each region of the weight grid corresponds to an area of the PF from the current scalarized solutions, then redistributes the weights accordingly. The method supports parallel, warm-started, inexact optimization with standard single-objective solvers. Theoretically, we establish that, under the stated regularity conditions, SURFACE achieves linear convergence of the preference distribution mismatch to a finite-resolution error floor of $\mathcal{O}(N^{-2/(M-1)})$, where $N$ is the number of adaptive weights and $M$ is the number of objectives. Empirically, experiments across multiple benchmarks demonstrate improved target-mass balance and PF coverage compared with established baselines.

papers.title: PF-Exec: Large-Scale UAV Relay Load Balancing with an Anchored Potential Direction Decider and a Per-Dimension Gain-Learning Executor
papers.abstract: Relay load balancing in large-scale UAV networks requires joint decisions on association, bandwidth, power and hovering position, while the dimension grows with the number of UAVs and each UAV sees only its local state. This paper splits the decision into two layers. An anchored potential direction decider emits a closed-form target at every instant and returns its direction only. A gain-learning executor maps a local observation into a positive gain per dimension, composes gain and target, and clips the action against the physical single-step bound; the two layers form PF-Exec. The unit gain is the default start, so the executor reduces to the pure potential policy before training. The load is first-order homogeneous in bandwidth, making the bandwidth target closed form, and the position target is the demand-weighted centroid of the served users. The system uses a two-hop access and millimetre-wave backhaul link with soft association, a 3GPP UMa-AV channel with two shadowing layers, an OU-type social-force crowd and a quadrotor physical layer. Evaluation spans all fleet sizes, two crowd scenarios, independent seeds, the published baselines in their own settings and a degraded-information line. In the highest-pressure burst setting the fixed-step comparison breaks down on part of the seeds, losing fairness and mean load at once, while PF-Exec holds fairness near one. Among the ten comparison methods only the greedy heuristic survives that setting; its load variance stays far higher. Under stale global state and position noise the fairness index stays high at both largest-scale scenarios. Flight energy is nearly identical between the learned and the fixed-step executor, and three constants are fixed once across all settings. The convergence properties of both layers, from the truncated gain iteration to the perturbed tracking bound, are proved in the companion analysis.

papers.title: Multifidelity Operator Inference for Dynamical Systems
papers.abstract: This paper presents a multifidelity (MF) formulation of Operator Inference (OpInf) for learning non-intrusive, physics-based reduced-order models (ROMs) of nonlinear dynamical systems. OpInf learns reduced operators from projections of snapshot data by solving a least squares regression problem. However, generating high-fidelity snapshots can be computationally expensive, limiting parameter coverage and the temporal extent of training trajectories for many aerospace applications, which can lead to inaccurate or unstable ROM predictions. This work proposes MF-OpInf, which combines limited high-fidelity snapshots with more plentiful low-fidelity snapshots through a control-variates-inspired MF least squares formulation to learn a single set of reduced operators across multiple trajectories. Low-fidelity trajectories provide additional parameter coverage and extend beyond the high-fidelity training time horizon. The low-fidelity snapshots are also used to construct an improved reduced basis through weighted proper orthogonal decomposition. We demonstrate MF-OpInf on a nonlinear reaction-diffusion problem with parametrized sinusoidal forcing and a two-dimensional incompressible flow past a cylinder with a parametrized inlet pulse. In these experiments, under an equal training simulation budget, MF-OpInf reduces the mean relative prediction error at unseen parameters by up to $87\%$ for the reaction-diffusion problem and $28\%$ for the cylinder flow problem over the test time regime, which extends beyond the high-fidelity training time horizon. These results demonstrate that MF-OpInf can improve temporal extrapolation and prediction at unseen parameters without increasing the training simulation budget.
papers.comments: 19 pages, AIAA SciTech Forum 2027 (Uncertainty Quantification Conference)

papers.title: Learning monotone game-theoretic linear MPC
papers.abstract: We propose a method to learn a game-theoretic model predictive control (GT-MPC) law by imitation from input and output data of a running multi-agent system. By interpreting the recorded inputs as the first moves of the equilibria of a game played by the agents, we learn the GT-MPC weights under hard input constraints and soft output constraints, without requiring the agents to reveal their objectives. We also impose that the resulting generalized Nash equilibrium (GNE) problem is strongly monotone, which ensures the existence and uniqueness of the equilibrium and, hence, that the learned GT-MPC law is well defined and can be evaluated efficiently online by variational GNE-seeking algorithms for linear-quadratic games. Moreover, strong monotonicity implies that the equilibrium is almost everywhere differentiable with respect to the references and the weights, which enables automatic differentiation for gradient-based optimization. In addition, we promote closed-loop stability of the unconstrained equilibrium feedback by incorporating a penalty that involves a jointly learned quadratic Lyapunov function. Learning a GT-MPC formulation enables us to explain the agents' objectives, reproduce their behavior in simulation in new scenarios, optimize their set-points, design mechanisms, and enforce additional constraints. A numerical example illustrates the approach.

papers.title: Red-Blue Hamiltonian Tomography via the Operator Lightcone Wavemap
papers.abstract: We introduce a model-free method for Hamiltonian tomography based on the operator spreading wavefront. Given two tensor network simulations of the same quantum lattice (one with the nominal Hamiltonian and one with one or more perturbed bonds), the signed cross-entropy of the non-identity Pauli weight field $\mathcal{L}(v,t) = -\ln(n_{\rm pert}/n_{\rm base})$ identifies each perturbed bond by its causal signature: a red-blue sign flip at the two endpoints, visible from the first wavefront crossing. Combining measurements from $p$ strategically placed observation centers via an ensemble log-likelihood sum, a single broken bond is identified with an 82-fold margin over the next candidate on a $7\times7$ lattice. Extending to realistic coupling degradation ($δJ = -0.20$) and up to 8 simultaneous faults, the integrated log-ratio $Λ(v) = \ln(\mathcal{B}(v)/\mathcal{N}(v))$ achieves a per-bond detection rate above 90\% in a single seismic pass using only 6 simulations. An iterative re-scan strategy progressively resolves multi-bond cases as the signal clears with each recalibration pass. The method requires no model assumptions and no knowledge of the perturbation type or magnitude; the detection is deliberately blind.

papers.title: Homogeneous pursuit in $β$ model
papers.abstract: Data in forms of networks has been encountered in various prevalent fields at the arrival of big data era. To unveil and recover the true model with core units with numerous links, the $β$-model under sparsity constraint is proposed to meet the expectation of statisticians and engineers. Not only does this network model inherit spectacular property from the Erdős-Rényi model, but also exhibits degree heterogeneity through tuning sparsity parameter $s$. In this paper, we propose Homogeneous Pursuit (HP), an $\ell_0$-constrained maximum likelihood estimation method implemented through a primal-dual algorithm. To ease the harshness of computation, we find the surrogate function of the corresponding objective function to derive Majorization Minimization algorithm through the primal-dual process. Moreover, after meticulous evaluation, the algorithm brought about captures the property of fine convergence rate in a contraction mapping way. Under some mild conditions, the proposed generalized information criterion (GIC$^*$) for selecting the sparsity level is consistent to find the truth. Combining HP with GIC$^*$ gives the adaptive procedure HP-GIC$^*$; HP-BIC denotes the same estimation method with sparsity selected by BIC. Finally, simulation studies show that GIC$^*$ improves support recovery relative to BIC in the reported comparisons, while HP achieves lower computational cost while maintaining estimation accuracy comparable to the sparse benchmark methods. A microfinance application illustrates the use of HP-GIC$^*$ for studying the association between network prominence and participation, with improved fit in the reported village-level regressions.

papers.title: Global saddle selection and exact absolute-instability boundaries for convection in porous media with throughflow
papers.abstract: In the Darcy-Prats problem, horizontal throughflow leaves the temporal onset of convection unchanged but raises the heating required for a localized disturbance to grow at a fixed point. The saddle equations give five candidates, but only the saddles reached by deformation of the Fourier contour contribute to the growth. For $Ra>π^2$, $Pe>0$ we prove that the same off-axis pair contributes throughout the domain: no Stokes transition can change its contribution. Its growth gives a unique analytic absolute threshold, first reached by the lowest vertical mode. Rescaling transfers the selection to Forchheimer drag, transverse rolls of a power-law fluid, anisotropic permeability, an open upper boundary and a vertical magnetic field. A shift of the same growth function accounts for interphase heat exchange in a model of metallic foam. At prescribed throughflow the threshold increases strictly with either resistance coefficient. In particular, a vertical magnetic field raises the absolute threshold at fixed Péclet number. Tabulated thresholds check the reduction. Algebraic elimination gives the boundary polynomial, and frequency recovery selects its physical branch. At the Darcy level the selected saddles trace an arc of the elliptic curve 11a3, a degeneration of a genus-two family at nonzero shifted levels. Series inversion on this arc gives an integer weak-throughflow series and an all-order strong-throughflow expansion. Rational certificates establish the exact convergence radii of both series on the selected sheets.

papers.title: Dynamical Gauss--Bonnet Sum Rules and Global Consistency in Five-Dimensional Braneworld Cosmology
authors: Paulo Michel Longo Tavares da Silva
papers.abstract: We derive an exact dynamical consistency relation for a smooth, periodically compactified five-dimensional Einstein--Gauss--Bonnet cosmology sourced by a real, minimally coupled canonical scalar field. For a spatially flat Friedmann--Lemaitre--Robertson--Walker slicing and a generally time-dependent warp factor, a contraction of the bulk equations eliminates both the scalar potential and the bulk cosmological constant. A direct orthonormal-curvature reconstruction gives the independent diagonal and mixed field equations and verifies the contracted Gauss--Bonnet identity. The integrated relation separates an exact total derivative from the dynamically active Lovelock sector. Importantly, satisfying the integrated sum rule alone does not imply a solution of the complete system. We prove that, for positive Gauss-Bonnet coupling, a smooth periodic time-independent warp factor and a canonical scalar exclude all exact expanding power-law scale factors $a(t)\propto t^p$ with $p>0$. This strengthens the previously established de Sitter sign obstruction and removes an earlier interpretation of $p=1/2$ as an admissible sign-compatible physical branch. For time-dependent warping, we reformulate bouncing conditions using proper time and the physical scale factor on each constant-$y$ hypersurface. We compare the common $w=-1$ geometric member with the perturbative weighted construction of Dias, Hoff da Silva, and da Rocha. At the level of the unexpanded Ricci-trace rearrangement, the curvature-only tensor contribution differs from the full Lanczos contraction by a definite scalar-curvature term. This distinction, and the additional independent field equations, delimit the physical conclusions that may be drawn from a necessary integrated condition.

papers.title: Scalar Entropic Damage Transport: Well-posed softening with a single damage variable
papers.abstract: Entropic Damage Transport (EDT) represents material softening via a local continuum damage model while ensuring the well-posedness of the mechanical boundary value problem. It is based on a convexification of the time-incremental potential associated with a rate-limited scalar damage model. A one-dimensional distribution of damage states serves as the internal variable, and the number of these states grows with the number of time steps. We show that the emergence of the damage distribution is an artifact of the time discretization. Surprisingly, the distribution concentrates at a single damage state in the time-continuous limit, and EDT converges to a rate-limited damage model with a scalar damage variable, whose free energy is jointly convex in the strain and the reciprocal degradation. We exploit this hidden convexity by a frozen-metric discretization in terms of the reciprocal degradation, which renders every increment jointly convex. The resulting scalar update preserves damage irreversibility, the prescribed damage-rate limitation and thermomechanical consistency, reduces to a scalar equation and provides a symmetric and positive definite algorithmic tangent in closed form. Computational experiments assess the accuracy and the efficiency of both formulations from the material point to the microstructure level, and demonstrate that the scalar update permits a finite-element computation of industrial size with more than 14 million degrees of freedom.
papers.comments: 42 pages, 15 figures. Submitted to Computer Methods in Applied Mechanics and Engineering

papers.title: Well-Posedness of Semimartingale Optimal Transport with Partial Marginal Constraints for Model Calibration
papers.abstract: We study the well-posedness and stability of a semimartingale optimal transport problem with partial marginal constraints at several maturities, motivated by the calibration of financial models to finitely many option prices. We connect its probabilistic and Eulerian formulations within the Benamou--Brenier framework. Under convex-duality assumptions, we establish strong duality for every price vector in the extended-value sense and existence of a primal optimizer whenever the value is finite. Under additional PDE assumptions, we establish dual attainment on the relative interior of the admissible price set, together with uniqueness of the primal optimizer. Under further non-degeneracy assumptions, we show that this price set has nonempty interior, on which the dual optimizer is unique and depends locally Lipschitz continuously on the prices. The analysis combines convex methods with regularity and local strong convexity results for Hamilton--Jacobi--Bellman solution maps established in a companion paper. For a fixed deterministic initial state, we also prove continuity of the optimal law on path space in the adapted Wasserstein distance of order two as prices vary within this interior. This stability concerns the optimizer over the full admissible class of semimartingale laws, allowing characteristics that depend on the past. The framework accommodates bounded uniformly continuous payoffs, including European puts in log-price coordinates, without payoff regularization or spatial truncation.

papers.title: Local Quantum Metrology: Precision Limits for Observers in QFT
papers.abstract: How precisely can an observer estimate a parameter related to a quantum field? This question is answered for quantum-mechanical systems using the SLD--Bures--Fisher metric and the quantum Cramér--Rao bound. However, local algebras in relativistic quantum field theory are of type III: they carry no trace and normal states have no density matrices, so the SLD quantum Fisher information and the quantum Cramér--Rao bound cannot be defined in the usual way. We define the SLD (Bures) quantum Fisher information on arbitrary von Neumann algebras through Uhlmann's transition probability and prove a quantum Cramér--Rao bound for collective measurements. We also show that the bound is sharp, and equals the largest classical Fisher information obtainable by measurements in the region.

papers.title: BeST: Beta splatted tomography for direct reconstruction from coherent imaging measurements
papers.abstract: Conventional coherent X-ray tomography requires the phase of each projection to be reconstructed with high fidelity. However, individual reconstructed projections might be flawed, e.g. due to positioning errors, yielding inconsistent tomographic reconstructions. By directly coupling phase retrieval and tomography, consistency is enforced through a common object volume. But reconstructing a full volume demands substantial computational resources. To reduce this demand, we introduce Beta Splatted Tomography (BeST), which represents the common object volume using compactly supported beta primitives with closed-form analytical projections, enabling efficient reconstruction directly from coherent scattering images. This representation substantially reduces the number of optimizable parameters compared to a voxel grid. We demonstrate BeST on experimental datasets from hard X-ray near-field holography and far-field ptychography measurements. In both cases, the joint technique improves reconstruction quality compared to two-step methods.

papers.title: The Exact Stabilization Time of Self-Stabilizing Coloring: Mean, Variance, and Distribution
papers.abstract: The worst-case stabilization time of a self-stabilizing algorithm usually says little about its typical behavior beyond the order of magnitude.
