papers.abstract: Let $G$ be a split Chevalley group of type $B_n$ ($n \geq 3$) or $D_n$ ($n \geq 4$), let $L$ be its Lie algebra and $Γ$ its long-root geometry, namely $Γ$ is the line-grassmannian of the polar space associated to $G$. It is well known that $L$ hosts a projective embedding of $Γ$, called the adjoint embedding, which realizes $Γ$ as a projective variety in the projective geometry of the underlying vector space of $L$. It is also known that $Γ$ admits the absolutely universal projective embedding, which is such that all projective embeddings of $Γ$ can be obtained from it as projections. When the field $F$ over which $G$ is defined is finite, the universal embedding of $Γ$ is just the same as the adjoint embedding. The same is not necessarily true when $F$ is infinite. Indeed, as we shall prove in this paper, the universal projective embedding of $Γ$ lives in a direct sum $K\oplus L$ for an $F$-vector space $K$, the dual of which is isomorphic to the derivation space $\mathrm{Der}(F)$ of $F$, which in general is non-trivial. Accordingly, the adjoint embedding of $Γ$ is universal if and only if $\mathrm{Der}(F)$ is trivial, namely $F$ is either perfect of positive characteristic or algebraic over its minimum subfield.

papers.title: Yang-Mills-Higgs Limits of Reflexive Higgs Sheaves
papers.abstract: For stable Higgs bundles, Hermitian-Einstein metrics can be obtained as limits of the Yang-Mills-Higgs (Y-M-H) flow. We study the algebraic structure of subsequential limits of this flow for reflexive Higgs sheaves over compact Kähler manifolds, without assuming stability. We prove that the limiting reflexive Higgs sheaf is isomorphic to the double dual of the graded sheaf associated with the Harder-Narasimhan-Seshadri filtration of the initial sheaf.

papers.title: DREAM: Delay-Resistant Acceleration with Momentum
papers.abstract: With exact, delay-free gradients, Nesterov's accelerated gradient (NAG) achieves optimal $\sqrtκ$ dependence for $L$-smooth, $μ$-strongly convex objectives, where $κ=L/μ$; heavy-ball (HB) achieves the same scaling on strongly convex quadratics. In asynchronous and distributed settings, gradients can be inexact, with delays varying across workers and iterations. We isolate staleness using a fixed delay $τ\ge1$, replacing $\nabla f(y_k)$ with $\nabla f(y_{k-τ})$ at iteration $k$. Arjevani, Shamir, and Srebro establish a worst-case lower bound of $Ω(τ\sqrtκ\log(1/\varepsilon))$ iterations to reach objective error at most $\varepsilon$ as $\varepsilon\to0$. We show that for any fixed positive delay, neither NAG nor HB retains $\sqrtκ$-acceleration on strongly convex quadratics when updating every iteration, for any stable constant step size and positive momentum. We introduce delay-resistant accelerated momentum (DREAM), which decouples gradient-query extrapolation from momentum and uses explicit delay-dependent parameters. DREAM attains a linear convergence rate $1-Θ(1/(τ\sqrtκ))$ for all smooth strongly convex objectives as $κ\to\infty$, yielding complexity matching the delayed first-order lower bound up to logarithmic factors. Our proof combines characteristic-polynomial stability analysis on quadratics with an analytic Zames--Falb integral quadratic constraint certificate. We extend DREAM to smooth convex objectives, obtaining near-optimal iteration complexity up to logarithmic factors for sufficiently small target accuracy. Experiments on strongly convex quadratics and regularized logistic regression corroborate DREAM's accelerated condition-number dependence under delay, unlike NAG and HB, and suggest this scaling persists when parameters use a conservative bound on the true delay.

papers.title: Symplectic Cuts and Moment Polyptychs of Hypertoric Varieties
papers.abstract: We study compact symplectic cuts of hypertoric varieties and characterise their smoothness. When the defining arrangement has a non-empty bounded base region, the fibre-rotation action has a proper moment map and gives compact Kähler orbifold cuts at regular levels. For a smooth hypertoric manifold, an outer-chamber cut, taken above the largest critical value of this moment map, is smooth if and only if the manifold is the cotangent bundle of its distinguished compact toric subvariety; that subvariety is then a product of projective spaces, and every positive level is regular with a smooth cut. If the compact core of a smooth hypertoric manifold is reducible, every outer-chamber cut has a boundary point with non-trivial cyclic isotropy and a singular coarse local quotient, whereas every cut below the smallest positive critical value is smooth. We introduce the moment polyptych, assembled from truncated arrangement regions, and recover the residual fixed points, tangent weights, and finite local groups from its edges and labelled lattice data. Restriction to arrangement flats is compatible with cutting and supplies the lower-dimensional models used in these calculations. The resulting local data are applied to equivariant quantisation in the companion paper (arXiv:2611.14090).
papers.comments: 28 pages, 6 figures. v4: abstract updated; v3: references added, minor edits; v2: the paper has been split into two parts; this is Part I, and the quantisation results of v1 will appear in Part II

papers.title: Point Corrections and Wall-Crossing Geometry on the Quintic del Pezzo Threefold
papers.abstract: We study wall crossing for ideal classes of rational curves of degrees two through five on the quintic del Pezzo threefold $X=V_5$. Wall exclusion and a uniform bound on the correction length rule out point corrections in degrees two through four on the outer segments of the negative zero-tilt-slope paths. In degree five a correction of length one occurs and gives rise to a second component of the good moduli space. For a rational outer stability parameter, this space is reduced and has exactly two irreducible components. The closure of the smooth rational-quintic locus is a normal tenfold. The other component is the smooth thirteenfold $X\times\mathrm{Gr}(2,7)$. Its points represent the polystable objects $I_{E_L}[1]\oplus\mathcal{O}_p$, where the pencil $L$ cuts out a quintic linear section $E_L$ of arithmetic genus one. The scheme-theoretic intersection is the normal determinantal ninefold parametrizing pairs $(p,L)$ for which $E_L$ is singular at $p$. Along their common reduced singular locus, the principal component and the intersection have transverse models given by the cones of $2\times4$ and $2\times3$ matrices of rank at most one, respectively. We construct a small resolution of the principal component as the projectivization of a rank-five extension bundle over the blow-up of the Altavilla--Petković--Rota sixfold along its point locus.

papers.title: Indecomposability of derived categories and nef canonical divisors in dimensions three and four
papers.abstract: We prove that a smooth projective threefold or fourfold whose bounded derived category admits no nontrivial semiorthogonal decomposition has nef canonical divisor, which establishes \cite[Conjecture~1.1]{KO2018} in these dimensions. The proof combines the classification of extremal contractions with constructions of nontrivial admissible subcategories. In dimension four, we refine the descriptions of isolated surface fibers and construct exceptional objects supported on certain fibers.
papers.comments: Update title and introduction, 26 pages, Comments are welcome

papers.title: Porosity in Diophantine approximation
papers.abstract: We provide a general framework for obtaining upper bounds on the packing dimension of certain sets arising from Diophantine approximation using the notion of porosity from geometric measure theory. In particular, the framework relies on showing that such sets are mean porous, as introduced by Koskela and Rohde (Math. Ann., 1997). As applications of our framework we show that: For $\varepsilon>0$ sufficiently small, the set of $d$-dimensional $\varepsilon$-badly approximable points has packing codimension comparable to $\varepsilon^{d}$ up to multiplicative constant. Any $C^{2}$ submanifold of $\mathbb{R}^{d}$ with bounded first and second partial derivatives intersected with the set of $d$-dimensional $\varepsilon$-badly approximable points has packing dimension strictly less than the dimension of the submanifold. For any matrix $A\in \mathbb{R}^{m\times n}$ satisfying certain Diophantine conditions, the set of points that avoid the $\varepsilon \|\mathbf{q}\|_{\infty}^{-\frac{n}{m}}$-neighbourhood of the orbit $\{A\mathbf{q} \mod \mathbb{Z}^{m}:\mathbf{q} \in \mathbb{Z}^{n}\}$ has packing codimension greater than $C_{A} \varepsilon^{m}$ for $C_{A}$ a constant depending on $A$ and $m$ only. \end{itemize}

papers.title: A Second-Order Stochastic Dynamic Mode Decomposition by Richardson Extrapolation
papers.abstract: Stochastic dynamic mode decomposition (SDMD) approximates the Koopman semigroup of an Itô diffusion by a Galerkin generator matrix on a dictionary of observables, computed from samples of the invariant law and generator evaluations, and advances observables with a first-order stochastic Taylor step (SDMD-1). The second-order Taylor step (SDMD-2) also needs a third matrix, a dictionary with four derivatives, and a fourth-order differential operator evaluated at every sample. Richardson extrapolation of the SDMD-1 step (SDMD-R) is second-order accurate with the data, the matrices, and the regularity of SDMD-1. The error bound, for exact and empirical matrices, consists of the Galerkin error of the dictionary, a time-stepping term, and a data term of order $m^{-1/2}$ in the sample size $m$. Relative to the Galerkin semigroup, the limit of the schemes as the time step $\dt\to0$, the time-stepping error is $O(\dt^2)$ for SDMD-R and $O(Θ_N\dt+\dt^2)$ for SDMD-2, with $Θ_N$ the norm of the second-order Galerkin residual $\Proj_N\cA(I-\Proj_N)\cA|_{\cV_N}$, and the first-order term is attained. For reversible periodic diffusions and trigonometric dictionaries with cutoff $K$, the step restriction $\dt\lesssim K^{-2}$ makes all three schemes contractions, and the error against the Koopman semigroup on $H^\ell$ observables is $O(K^{-(\ell-2)}+\dt^p)$ plus a data term of order $K^{d+2}(m^{-1}\log K)^{1/2}$ in dimension $d$, with $p=1$ for SDMD-1 and $p=2$ for SDMD-R and SDMD-2. In experiments with trigonometric dictionaries the errors of SDMD-R and SDMD-2 differ by at most ten percent. For a spline dictionary with two derivatives, SDMD-R remains second-order accurate, whereas SDMD-2 with pointwise evaluations is first-order accurate.

papers.title: Improved Berezin--Li--Yau Bounds for Dirichlet Eigenvalues via Fourier Coupling and Frequency Concentration
papers.abstract: Let $0<λ_1\leqλ_2\leq\cdots$ be the Dirichlet eigenvalues of an open set $Ω\subset\mathbb R^n$, $n\geq2$. We develop two Fourier-space refinements of the Berezin--Li--Yau argument. For every finite-measure open set, coordinate commutator identities and coupled scalar--vector projections lead to a one-dimensional variational constant $C_n^{\mathrm{new}}$ and the individual bound \[ λ_k\geq C_n^{\mathrm{new}}(2π)^2ω_n^{-2/n} |Ω|^{-2/n}k^{2/n}, \qquad \frac{n}{n+2}<c_n^{\mathrm{env}}<C_n^{\mathrm{new}}<1. \] Here $n/(n+2)$ is the classical Li--Yau individual coefficient and $c_n^{\mathrm{env}}$ is the coefficient associated with the uncoupled scalar envelope developed in our previous paper. Thus the displayed strict hierarchy separates the gain of the scalar energy envelope from the further gain supplied by the commutator coupling. For bounded open sets, a frequency-concentration operator, its first two traces, and the Ky Fan principle force Fourier mass outside the Li--Yau filling ball. A two-region bathtub argument then gives \[ \sum_{j=1}^kλ_j \geq \mathcal C_k^{(2)}(Ω) \frac{n}{n+2}(2π)^2ω_n^{-2/n} |Ω|^{-2/n}k^{1+2/n}, \qquad \mathcal C_k^{(2)}(Ω)>1, \] where $\mathcal C_k^{(2)}(Ω)$ is strictly decreasing in $k$ and converges to one, and \[ \mathcal C_k^{(2)}(Ω)-1\geq \frac{n+2}{2(n+1)^2} \left(\frac{ω_{n-1}}{ω_n}\right)^2 \left(\frac34\right)^{n-1}k^{-2/n}. \] Thus the sharp leading term in the Berezin--Li--Yau sum is supplemented by an explicit positive, volume-only correction of order $k$. Apart from boundedness in the concentration argument, no boundary regularity, convexity, or connectedness is assumed. These improvements do not prove Pólya's conjecture: the individual coefficient is below one, and the sum multiplier tends to one.

papers.title: Short permutation pattern waves: The complete length-five classification
papers.abstract: For a permutation pi in Sk, a pi-wave is an increasing sequence of integers whose consecutive gaps have relative order pi. Let g(pi, n) be the maximum cardinality of a pi-wave-free subset of [n], and let P(pi, r) be the least integer N such that every r-coloring of [N] contains a monochromatic pi-wave. We determine the asymptotic orders of both functions for every permutation of length at most five. Existing upper bounds and weak-wave constructions provide sharp bounds for all but eight length-five patterns in S_5. For these eight exceptional alternating patterns, we establish g(pi, n) = Theta((log n)squared) and P(pi, r) = Theta(r(log r)squared).

papers.title: Every obstruction to noncontextual hidden variables is finite: well-founded refutations in infinitary real-valued logic
papers.abstract: We study the obstructions to noncontextual hidden variables when quantum probability is described in full, by the complete lattice of closed subspaces of a separable infinite-dimensional Hilbert space together with its countably additive measures. We give such a description in infinitary real-valued logic, the infinitary extension of Keisler's model theory of general structures; the countable suprema and infima of this logic express the completeness of the lattice and the countable additivity of the measures. The standard models of our axioms represent exactly the density-operator measures of Gleason's theorem. The axioms are closed conditions, non-strict inequalities between the values of sentences and rational numbers. The expressive power afforded by infinitary sentences comes at the price of compactness. The hypothesis that at each hidden state every event receives the value 0 or 1, whatever the context of measurement, contradicts the axioms, yet it is consistent with every finite subset of them. The obstructions nevertheless remain finite. We prove that in this logic a countable set of closed conditions is inconsistent if and only if a well-founded tree whose branches end in finite contradictions refutes it; for the hypothesis above, every such tree has an infinitely branching node. The finiteness theorem is therefore maximal: a hidden-variable hypothesis expressed by countably many closed conditions is inconsistent with the axioms, and thus an obstruction, exactly when such a tree refutes the hypothesis together with the axioms. The same language defines, uniformly across standard models, exactly the $σ$-projective sets of probabilities, and all these results are proved in ZFC.

papers.title: Poissonian Pair Correlation and Discrepancy Rates
papers.abstract: We prove the existence of a sequence in $[0,1)$ with Poissonian pair correlation (PPC) and optimal-order star discrepancy $D_N^*=O((\log N)/N)$, and further give a deterministic construction by applying a conditional-expectation rule to a nested dyadic random model. We also show that PPC imposes no universal discrepancy decay rate: for every positive sequence $ρ_N\to0$, there exists a PPC sequence with $D_N^*/ρ_N\to\infty$. Under suitable regularity and growth assumptions, we realize prescribed discrepancy asymptotics, including $D_N^*\sim c_βN^{-β}$ for every $0<β<1$, with $c_β>0$. We further construct a PPC sequence satisfying $D_N^*\asymp(\log N)/N$ for all sufficiently large $N$.

papers.title: Lyapunov spectrum, Harder--Narasimhan filtration and thin monodromy
papers.abstract: We study the equality case of the inequalities between the Lyapunov spectrum and the Harder--Narasimhan slopes of a semi-simple local system with non-expanding cusp monodromy over a finite-area hyperbolic surface. This gives a nonlattice-transversality alternative of the monodromy group. On the other hand, we generalize Filip's Assumptions A and B to give classes of polarized variation of Hodge structures that achieve the equality. As an application, we recover the thinness of C-32 in $\mathrm{Sp}_6\mathbb{R}$. Besides, we provide an upper bound, called average Cartan spectrum, that dominates the Lyapunov spectrum and study its rigidity.
papers.comments: Update several references. 63 pages,including a declaration of AI use, comments are very welcome

papers.title: Construction of entropies for cross-diffusion systems
papers.abstract: The analysis of cross-diffusion systems with nonsymmetric and indefinite diffusion matrices often relies on the existence of entropies, that is, Lyapunov functionals whose dissipation often yields gradient estimates. We propose a general strategy for constructing entropies for two-species cross-diffusion systems, based on the assumption that the mobility matrix is symmetric, in accordance with Onsager's reciprocal relations. The symmetry condition leads to a linear hyperbolic equation in two variables, which can be reformulated as a linear transport system along the eigendirections of the diffusion matrix, related to the approach of Jenssen and Kogan for hyperbolic conservation laws. Positive solutions to this system yield a family of entropies parametrized by two arbitrary functions of one variable. Sufficient conditions for their existence on (possibly unbounded) characteristic rectangles are given, the mechanisms that may prevent the existence of an entropy are identified, and systems without any entropy structure are presented. The general construction recovers known entropies for models arising in physics and biology and provides new ones. For systems with an arbitrary number of components, we derive sufficient conditions for the existence of separable entropies and give a rank criterion for the uniqueness of entropies (up to affine functions). Cross-diffusion systems without symmetry of the mobility matrix are also discussed.

papers.title: Neyman Orthogonalized Specification Tests for Conditional Tail Index Models
papers.abstract: We develop specification tests for parametric conditional tail index models of heavy-tailed distributions. The tests are based on a projected empirical process that removes the first-order effect of estimating the null parameter. Within the conditional Hall class, we identify conditions under which projection also eliminates the leading Pareto approximation bias in the test process, permitting lower thresholds while preserving asymptotically correct size. We establish the validity of the tests via multiplier bootstrap and characterize power against fixed and local alternatives. For log-linear models, bootstrap validity extends to settings in which covariates of observations above a common threshold concentrate and the smallest eigenvalue of the information matrix tends to zero. We further propose a novel threshold selection rule based on an estimate of the Pareto approximation bias after projection. The rule uses the estimated bias to determine whether a reference threshold can be lowered to retain more observations, with potential gains in power. The finite sample performance of the tests is examined through simulations and a real data application.

papers.title: A Trivalent Graph of Girth 14 and Order 372
papers.abstract: The smallest known trivalent graph of girth 14 is constructed. The graph has 372 vertices, improving the old upper bound of 384 \cite{exoo14}. The construction uses methods that may be new to this problem.

papers.title: Supercuspidal, discrete, and elliptic densities for reductive groups over non-archimedean local fields
papers.abstract: Let $G$ be the group of points of a connected reductive group over a non-archimedean local field $F$ of arbitrary characteristic, with residue field of size $q$. For a principal congruence tower $K_n$ attached to a Lie algebra lattice $\mathcal{L}$, the supercuspidal and discrete series proportions of the Plancherel mass of the $K_n$-fixed vectors both converge, with error $O(q^{-n/4})$, to the probability that a Haar-random form in the dual lattice $Λ=\mathcal{L}^\vee$ is elliptic. For $\mathrm{GL}_d$, the supercuspidal limit confirms a prediction of Howe. This probability is positive, and we characterize when it is one. More generally, outside a union of congruence cells of total mass $O(q^{-n/4})$, each cell determines a common Levi class for the supercuspidal and discrete series supports of every tempered representation containing its character. The limiting mass of each class is the probability that a Haar-random form in $Λ$ lies in the corresponding stratum. The proof combines finite Fourier analysis, quantitative estimates for parabolic incidence maps, and a Jacquet-module argument that detects unitary exponents.
papers.comments: 54 pages. Extended to discrete series densities and the distribution of Levi support classes; title and abstract updated

papers.title: Costate-Conditioned Dynamic Programming for Parallel-in-Time Solution of Equality-Constrained Optimal Control Problems
papers.abstract: Gradient based trajectory optimisation algorithms spend most of their per-iteration time on a structured Newton--KKT system. The system corresponds to an equality-constrained linear-quadratic optimal control problem and dedicated Riccati-type solvers exhibit linear complexity in the horizon length. Parallel-in-time algorithms exhibit the potential to reduce the complexity to logarithmic in the horizon by distributing several subtrajectories over multiple cores and then stitch together the results by means of an associative scan. Existing exact formulations condition each subtrajectory on its terminal state. Each subproblem then carries the reachability to that terminal state explicitly as constraint rows. The associated reachability decision however is ill-conditioned for weakly actuated systems. In this work we condition each subtrajectory on the terminal costate instead. The resulting subproblems can now be computed by a free-end Riccati recursion without reachability carrying rows. This approach effectively compensates for the ill-conditioning of weakly actuated systems but requires additional bookkeeping with Lagrangian multipliers when stitching together the various subproblems. Numerically the method reproduces a direct solution of the primal-dual Newton-KKT system to $10^{-12}$ in relative terms, on a weakly controllable chain of masses. The accurracy rivals that of a sequential recursion, whereas terminal-state conditioning loses up to six digits or fails. Operation counts on a problem with 64 subtrajectories and a horizon of 4096 stages gives a speed-up of 26 compared with a sequential solve.

papers.title: Pointwise estimates for an anisotropic product type singular integral on the sphere
On transition probabilities for the ASEP on the half-line
papers.abstract: We study the asymmetric simple exclusion process on the half-line with particle insertion and no particle removal at the boundary. We point out that there exist two distinct multiple contour integral formulas for the transition probability between two finite particle configurations containing the same number of particles. We recall one of these formulas from the literature and prove a second, new formula by showing that it satisfies the evolution equation using a coordinate Bethe ansatz calculation and verify that the initial condition is implemented by the contour integrals. As an application we sum this formula over all final configurations and obtain an integral formula for the probability that the number of particles is conserved up to a given time. The proofs use symmetric rational functions and their properties together with contour deformations.

papers.title: Coarse Embeddings Beyond Doubling: Persistence Diagrams and Multiparameter Modules
papers.abstract: We study coarse embeddings into Hilbert space and the asymptotic dimension of spaces of persistence diagrams and multiparameter persistence modules. We build coarse embeddings from admissible tent covers of bounded multiplicity at every scale, which doubling spaces carry but which do not require doubling: stacking them across dyadic scales gives an explicit $1$-Lipschitz coarse embedding, with lower gauge $c\sqrt{τt}$, or nearly linear for slowly decaying weights, and the same covers bound the asymptotic dimension by the multiplicity. The spaces of persistence diagrams are not doubling but carry such covers, and for diagrams with at most $n$ points our covers improve the constant of the known landmark embedding by a factor exponential in $n$. Slice by slice, the construction embeds multiparameter modules with boundedly many bars per slice under the matching distance on any finite net of slices, a class that contains the modules with at most $n$ generators. Under the continuous distances, bounding bars or persistent Betti numbers does not suffice: two-parameter modules with one bar on every slice have infinite asymptotic dimension, and neither they nor the modules of bounded support and bounded rank admit a coarse embedding into Hilbert space, under the matching or the interleaving distance.

papers.title: Entropy maximization for cube projections
papers.abstract: We prove that, in every dimension $n\ge150$, the one-dimensional projections of the uniform distribution on a cube have the largest differential entropy in directions with equal coordinate magnitudes. This establishes the conjecture of Eskenazis, Nayar, and Tkocz in these dimensions.

papers.title: Face lattices of polytopes and bipolar polytopes
papers.abstract: We show that the face lattice of every convex polytope $Q$ is, on the combinatorial level, the vertex set of a polytope one dimension higher: the faces of $Q$ are the vertices of a \emph{bipolar polytope} $W(\mathcal{F}(Q))$, and the intervals of the face lattice are its faces. Here a bipolar polytope is a polytope with two distinguished vertices, the poles, such that every facet contains exactly one of them and an intersection property holds. The vertices of every bipolar polytope carry a lattice order whose intervals are the faces, and this lattice is the face lattice of the vertex figure at either pole; conversely, every atomistic and coatomistic lattice that is an abstract polytope arises in this way. Geometrically, the polar of the Cayley polytope of $Q$ and $Q^\circ$ is a convex realization of $W(\mathcal{F}(Q))$ whenever the normal fan and the face fan of $Q$ satisfy a certain interval condition; this holds for cubes and cross-polytopes and for suitable realizations of all polytopes of dimension at most three. Finally, every combinatorial type of $3$-polytope has a realization that decomposes into convex bipolar polytopes, one for each vertex.
papers.comments: 30 pages, 6 Figures, to be submitted in Journal of Combinatorial Theory, Series A v2: references updated, figures improved for greyscale printing

papers.title: Quasi-equatorial controlled switching in inertial magnetization dynamics
papers.abstract: We design exponentially decaying transverse magnetic fields for reliable and ultra-fast (picosecond) magnetization reversal governed by the inertial Landau--Lifshitz--Gilbert equation. The control construction uses an explicitly resolvable auxiliary model to select the field amplitude and characterize the influence of its decay rate, with the aim of obtaining reversal followed by relaxation without requiring a precisely timed interruption of the excitation. The auxiliary model is obtained through an equatorial approximation, and bounds on its latitude identify a regime consistent with quasi-equatorial motion. For the full nonlinear macrospin dynamics, an energy argument accounting for both inertial kinetic energy and the remaining field input provides a sufficient condition excluding backhopping, even while the exponential tail remains applied. Approximate confinement times and optimal decay rates are derived from the competition between field decay and inertial relaxation. Numerical simulations confirm the usefulness of these design estimates and identify their limitations near a capture boundary, where nearby pulses can lead to opposite final states. Spatially resolved inertial micromagnetic simulations further support reversal followed by relaxation over the simulated interval and quantify the transient departures from spatially coherent motion. The resulting approach combines explicit pulse design with a full-system energy certificate, while distinguishing rapid initial rotation from safe confinement and subsequent relaxation.

papers.title: Thales's theorem in higher dimensions
papers.abstract: In the Euclidean plane, Thales's theorem is equivalent to the statement that a quadrilateral with two opposite right angles has a circumscribed circle. We generalize the latter to higher dimensions: a convex polytope with two distinguished vertices, the \emph{poles}, such that the faces spanned by the two poles are perpendicular, is inscribed in the sphere whose diameter joins its poles. These \emph{orthogonally bipolar} polytopes are exactly the bipolar polytopes of a companion paper that arise as cutouts by orthogonal projections. As an application we show that for a polytope $P$ and a point $B$, the balls with diameters $[V,B]$, $V$ a vertex of $P$, cover $P$, and that the power diagram of their boundary spheres refines this covering to a tiling. Further, we investigate the properties of orthogonally bipolar polytopes, their characterization, and their application to tilings: in dimension three, the cutouts of $P$ by the orthogonal projections of $B$ onto its faces tile $P$ by orthogonally bipolar polytopes exactly when every such projection lies in the relative interior of its face. Finally, we propose an interpretation of the topic in political science.
papers.comments: 23 pages, 6 figures V2: references updated, figures improved for greyscale printing

papers.title: The bias interval of the elephant random walk
papers.abstract: Guérin, Laulin, Raschel, and Simon conjectured that the initial biases giving the superdiffusive elephant random walk a bimodal limit law form an interval centered at one half, and they described the problem as challenging. We prove this. For every superdiffusive memory, strongly biased starts are unimodal, and the limit density has two local maxima exactly when the bias lies in a proper open interval. Outside it, including its endpoints, the density has a unique local maximum. The interval is nonempty exactly above a single memory threshold, numerically about $0.6688$, whose uniqueness follows from a positive-weight integral for the central curvature of the fair-start density. We control sign changes in the finite walk's first and second differences, including those created at the boundary, and pass them to the limit. The bias boundary is continuous and tends to zero at least quadratically fast as memory tends to one.
papers.comments: 28 pages, 2 figures. Code, certificates and Lean files: https://github.com/apemm/elephant-bias-interval

papers.title: $\mathbb Z$ is diophantine over $\mathbb Q$ with 26 unknowns
papers.abstract: Recently, OpenAI proved that Hilbert's Tenth Problem over the field $\mathbb Q$ of rational numbers has a negative solution. Motivated by this work, G. Conant et al. showed that $\mathbb Z$ is diophantine over $\mathbb Q$, i.e., there is an integer-coefficient polynomial $F(x,y_1,\ldots,y_n)$ such that for any $x\in\mathbb Q$ we have $$ x\in\mathbb Z\quad\iff \exists\,y_1,\ldots,y_{n}\in\mathbb Q\ [F(x,y_1,\ldots,y_{n})=0].$$ They constructed such a polynomial $F$ with $°F=4$ and $n=221$.In this paper, we prove the existence of such a polynomial $F$ with $n=26$. We also show that $16$ existential unknowns suffice under the $abc$-conjecture.
papers.comments: 39 pages. Reduce 28 variables to 26 variables, and add Theorem 1.2

papers.title: Rational isogenies of rank-two Drinfeld modules
papers.abstract: We determine the $\mathbb{F}_{q}(T)$-rational points on the Drinfeld modular curves $X_{0}(\mathfrak{n})$ of arbitrary level, obtaining a complete classification of rational cyclic isogenies of rank-two Drinfeld $\mathbb{F}_{q}[T]$-modules over $\mathbb{F}_{q}(T)$. As consequences, we prove Schweizer's conjecture on rational torsion, establish optimal uniform bounds on the number of isomorphism classes in an $\mathbb{F}_{q}(T)$-isogeny class of rank-two Drinfeld $\mathbb{F}_{q}[T]$-modules and determine the geometric automorphism groups of $X_{0}(\mathfrak{p})$ for primes $\mathfrak{p}$ of degree at least three.

papers.title: Ehrhart Series and Transfer Matrices for Period-Two Polytopes with Consecutive Inequalities
papers.abstract: We study a family of period-two polytopes that can be naturally realized as lattice polytopes. In contrast to polytopes defined by a uniform system of inequalities, this family is characterized by consecutive coordinate inequalities whose bounds alternate between $s+1$ and $s$. The lattice points of these polytopes admit an explicit transfer-matrix formulation, which provides an effective framework for their enumeration and analysis. Furthermore, by considering fixed dilations, we investigate the associated dimensional generating functions and derive rational forms for the generating functions of the lattice points in the $m$-th dilates of the polytopes.

papers.title: Splitting Number at Singular Cardinals
papers.abstract: We study the splitting number at singular cardinals with emphasis on what we call the reduction to the cofinality problem: whether $\mathfrak{s}_κ = \mathfrak{s}_{\mathrm{cf}(κ)}$ holds for a singular cardinal $κ$. Our main tool is the transfinite logarithm function $\mathrm{log}_{2}(μ) := \min \{ λ\in \mathrm{card} \colon μ\leq 2^λ \}$ defined for every infinite cardinal $μ$. We prove that the reduction holds, and in fact $\mathfrak{s}_κ = \mathrm{log}_{2}(\mathrm{cf}(κ))$, whenever $\mathrm{cf}(κ)$ is uncountable and not weakly compact. When $\mathrm{cf}(κ) = \aleph_{0}$, we show that $\mathfrak{s}_κ = \mathfrak{s}$ provided that $\mathfrak{s} \leq \log_{2}(κ)$, while the failure of the reduction is consistent with $\mathrm{ZFC}$. When $\mathrm{cf}(κ)$ is weakly compact, we use a model constructed by Ben-Neria and Gitik to prove that, under suitable large cardinals hypothesis, $\mathfrak{s}_κ < \mathfrak{s}_{\mathrm{cf}(κ)}$ is consistent. Furthermore, we show that the consistency strength of $\mathrm{ZFC} \, +$"$\exists κ\in \mathrm{card} [\mathrm{cf}(κ) > \aleph_{0} \wedge \mathfrak{s}_κ < \mathfrak{s}_{\mathrm{cf}(κ)}]$'' is at least that of the negation of the singular cardinal hypothesis. Finally, we study the cofinality of $\mathfrak{s}_κ$, extending several results about the cofinality of $\mathfrak{s}$ to the uncountable setting. In particular, we show in $\mathrm{ZFC}$ that there are regular cardinals $κ$ such that $\mathfrak{s}_κ$ is singular, partially answering an open question posed by Fischer and Soukup.

papers.title: Nagata dimension, separation modulus and stochastic embeddings into trees
papers.abstract: The separation modulus of a metric space, introduced by Bartal in 1996, is related to different notions of dimensionality. Most generally, Naor and Silberman gave in 2011 an upper bound on the separation modulus in terms of Nagata dimension. We prove that this bound cannot be reversed; that is, there are metric spaces with arbitrarily high Nagata dimension and stochastically embeddable into trees with uniform distortion, which therefore have uniformly bounded separation modulus. Similarly, we construct spaces with arbitrarily high Nagata dimension whose spaces of probability measures endowed with the Earth Mover's Distance (equivalently, their Lipschitz-free spaces) are embeddable into $L_1$ with uniformly bounded distortion. By gluing these spaces together, we obtain infinite Nagata dimensional metric spaces whose separation modulus is finite and whose Lipschitz-free space is isomorphic to $\ell_1$, respectively. Finally, we provide relations between separation modulus and stochastic embeddability into trees, also known as random approximability by tree metrics, in particular for the case of snowflake metrics.

papers.title: GV-subschemes and hyperelliptic Jacobians
papers.abstract: We provide a solution to the hyperelliptic Schottky problem: a principally polarized complex abelian variety whose theta divisor has singular locus of codimension three is a hyperelliptic Jacobian. As a key step towards this criterion for hyperelliptic Jacobians, we prove a conjecture of Pareschi and Popa which predicts that if the ideal sheaf $I_X$ of a subscheme $X$ of an indecomposable PPAV $(A, Θ)$ satisfies that $I_X(2Θ)$ is IT$_0$, then $X$ is a GV-subscheme. As a corollary of the main result, the base scheme of an ample line bundle on a complex abelian variety is generically reduced along every irreducible component of codimension $2$, confirming a conjecture of Debarre. This corollary completes the algebro-geometry proof by Arbarello-Codogni-Pareschi in \cite{ACP21, ACP25} of Novikov's conjecture, which characterizes Jacobians via the KP equation.

papers.title: $(r,s)$-Designs in the Nonbinary Johnson Scheme: Constructions and Linear Codes
papers.abstract: Using factorizations of complete graphs, we determine the existence conditions for $(2,1)$-designs in the nonbinary Johnson scheme where each $3$-element subset appears exactly once as a support. Furthermore, by utilizing large sets of Steiner triple systems, we construct designs with index $1$ that cannot be obtained from the known construction combining block designs and orthogonal arrays. For linear codes, we express multiplicative character sums over specified nonzero coordinates as sums over the codewords of the dual code. Using this identity along with the rank of a matrix formed by Krawtchouk polynomials, we provide a sufficient condition for the set of all codewords of a given weight to form an $(r,s)$-design. In this matrix, we can utilize not only the rows corresponding to weights absent from the code, but also the rows corresponding to weights for which the set of codewords already forms a design. Moreover, let $q>2$ be a prime power, and let $0 \neq C \subsetneq \mathbb{F}_q^n$ be a linear code with exactly two nonzero weights. For $t \geq 2$, the set of all codewords of weight $w \geq t$ forms a non-empty $(t,t)$-design if and only if the dual minimum distance is at least $t+2$. Consequently, this provides a negative answer to the Wu--Zhou problem concerning two-weight codes with a dual minimum distance of $3$.

papers.title: Rings with unequal $\operatorname{silp-spli}$
papers.abstract: For a unital associative ring $R$, let $\operatorname{silp}(R)$ be the supremum of the injective dimensions of all projective right $R$-modules, and let $\operatorname{spli}(R)$ be the supremum of the projective dimensions of all injective right $R$-modules. We construct an explicit non-Noetherian unital algebra \[R=k1\oplus \frac{k(0\longrightarrow1\longrightarrow2\longrightarrow\cdots)} {\langle\text{all paths of length }2\rangle}\] over any field and prove that $\operatorname{silp}(R)=1$ and $\operatorname{spli}(R)=\infty. $ The algebra is the unitization of the non-unital path algebra of the one-sided infinite ray modulo paths of length two. The example answers the question whether $\operatorname{silp=spli}$ raised by Gedrich and Gruenberg.

papers.title: Engineering Yeast Cells to Facilitate Information Exchange
papers.abstract: Although continuous advances in theoretical modelling of Molecular Communications (MC) are observed, there is still an insuperable gap between theory and experimental testbeds, especially at the microscale. In this paper, the development of the first testbed incorporating engineered yeast cells is reported. Different from the existing literature, eukaryotic yeast cells are considered for both the sender and the receiver, with α-factor molecules facilitating the information transfer. The use of such cells is motivated mainly by the well understood biological mechanism of yeast mating, together with their genetic amenability. In addition, recent advances in yeast biosensing establish yeast as a suitable detector and a neat interface to in-body sensor networks. The system under consideration is presented first, and the mathematical models of the underlying biological processes leading to an end-to-end (E2E) system are given. The experimental setup is then described and used to obtain experimental results which validate the developed mathematical models. Beyond that, the ability of the system to effectively generate output pulses in response to repeated stimuli is demonstrated, reporting one event per two hours. However, fast RNA fluctuations indicate cell responses in less than three minutes, demonstrating the potential for much higher rates in the future.
papers.comments: 18 pages, 9 figures (2 of which are not colored) all .png, recently accepted for publication at TMBMC

papers.title: Random Abstract Cell Complexes
papers.abstract: In machine learning and signal processing, methods based on (abstract) cell complexes (CCs) are being applied successfully in different applications. However, there is currently a lack of random models, which are necessary for a thorough evaluation of these methods, both by generating synthetic data and as null models to compare results to. We fill this gap by defining a random model for abstract cell complexes based on independent inclusion probabilities, similar to the Erdős-Rényi model for graphs. We also discuss how modifications to bias the model to incorporate more structure can be implemented. The model can also be used to lift a graph (or other cell complex) to a cell complex of arbitrary dimension. The main challenge in this is that the number of cycles (possible 2-cells) on graphs is exponential, and the same is true in higher dimensions. We overcome this complexity with an approximate sampling algorithm limited to 2-cells (polygons) that is based on a recent advance in sampling cycles on a graph. Using this algorithm, we analyze the properties of random 2-dimensional CCs and showcase its usage as a performance baseline for both topological signal processing and topological deep learning. The algorithm is available in the package py-raccoon on the Python Package Index.
papers.comments: 9 pages, 7 figures (plus appendix). For evaluation code, see https://github.com/josefhoppe/random-abstract-cell-complexes

papers.title: An 'Experimental Mathematics' Approach to Stolarsky Interspersions via Automata Theory
papers.abstract: We look at the Stolarsky interspersions (such as the Wythoff array) one more time, this time using tools from automata theory. These tools allow easy verification of many of the published results on these arrays, as well as proofs of new results.
papers.comments: This revision fixes up numerous typographical errors and adds some new results

papers.title: Evaluating the Generalizability and Explainability of Firn Image Classification with Topological Features
papers.abstract: In this paper we evaluate the performance of topological features for generalizable and explainable classification of firn image data, with the broader goal of understanding the advantages, pitfalls, and trade-offs in topological featurization. Firn refers to layers of granular snow within glaciers that haven't yet been compressed into ice. This compaction process imposes distinct topological and geometric structure on firn that varies with depth within the firn column. However, the limited and highly correlated training data available results in naive classifiers (such as convolutional neural networks) overfitting to orientation-dependent features. This motivates us to evaluate topological data analysis (TDA) as a way to design features which capture the shape of the firn data while retaining a large degree of invariance. We evaluate two classes of topological features, sublevel set features and distance transform features, together with persistence curves, to predict sample depth from firn images. A range of challenging training-test scenarios reveals that no one choice of method dominates in all categories. In particular, we see a tradeoff between accuracy on the one hand, and generalizability and explainability (via feature importance) on the other.
papers.comments: Extended version with additional experiments on generalizability and explainability

papers.title: Two Tiling is Undecidable
papers.abstract: We show that the following problem is undecidable: given two polygonal prototiles, determine whether the plane can be tiled with rotated and translated copies of them. This improves a result of Demaine and Langerman [SoCG 2025], who showed undecidability for three tiles. Along the way, we show that tiling with one prototile is undecidable if there can be edge-to-edge matching rules. This is the first result to show undecidability for monotiling with only local matching constraints.

papers.title: Recovering the Euclidean Geometry of High-Dimensional Data Under Heterogeneous Noise
papers.abstract: Pairwise Euclidean distances provide a simple geometric representation of high-dimensional data and underlie many data analysis methods, including clustering, visualization, and manifold learning. However, in real-world applications, these distances can be severely corrupted by heterogeneous noise, where different data points are subject to different, and potentially large, noise levels. Such noise distorts the distances inhomogeneously, leading to a misrepresentation of the underlying data geometry. In this work, we ask whether the underlying clean Euclidean geometry can nevertheless be recovered from the corrupted pairwise distances. We answer this question affirmatively, showing that, perhaps surprisingly, such recovery is possible across a broad class of high-dimensional settings with underlying low-dimensional geometry, even when the noise magnitudes vary substantially across observations. We develop a principled approach for recovering the clean pairwise distances, without prior knowledge of either the clean data structure or the noise distribution, and establish probabilistic recovery guarantees. In particular, the recovery error converges to zero at polynomial rates as the feature dimension and dataset size increase simultaneously. Experiments on synthetic datasets demonstrate accurate recovery of the Euclidean geometry in challenging regimes and improved robustness of downstream methods that rely on pairwise distances. When applied to real single-cell RNA sequencing data, our method reliably recovers local neighborhood structure, enabling accurate nearest-neighbor identification used in many downstream analyses.

papers.title: On the Parameterized Complexity of Grundy Domination and Zero Forcing Problems
papers.abstract: We consider two different problem families that deal with domination in graphs. On the one hand, we focus on dominating sequences. In such a sequence, every vertex dominates some vertex of the graph that was not dominated by any earlier vertex in the sequence. The problem of finding the longest dominating sequence is known as $\mathsf{Grundy~Domination}$. Depending on whether the closed or the open neighborhoods are used for domination, there are three other versions of this problem: $\mathsf{Grundy~Total~Domination}$, $\mathsf{L\text{-}Grundy~Domination}$, and $\mathsf{Z\text{-}Grundy~Domination}$. We show that all four problem variants are $\mathsf{W[1]}$-complete when parameterized by the solution size. On the other hand, we consider the family of zero forcing problems which form the parametric duals of the Grundy domination problems. In these problems, one looks for the smallest set of vertices initially colored blue such that certain color change rules are able to color all other vertices blue. It has been shown that the dual of $\mathsf{Z\text{-}Grundy~Domination}$, known as $\mathsf{Zero~Forcing~Set}$, is in $\mathsf{FPT}$ when parameterized by the treewidth or the solution size. We extend the treewidth result to the other three variants of zero forcing and their respective Grundy domination problems. Our algorithm also implies an $\mathsf{FPT}$ algorithm for $\mathsf{Grundy~Domination}$ when parameterized by the number of vertices that are not in the dominating sequence. In contrast, we show that $\mathsf{L\text{-}Grundy~Domination}$ is $\mathsf{W[1]}$-hard for that parameter.
papers.comments: version published in the Journal of Computer and System Sciences
papers.journal_ref: Journal of Computer and System Sciences 164, Article 103875 (2027)

papers.title: Bayesian Transfer Operators in Reproducing Kernel Hilbert Spaces
papers.abstract: Transfer operators provide a linear description of nonlinear dynamical systems by propagating observables or probability distributions. In reproducing kernel Hilbert spaces, these operators are represented through conditional mean embeddings, whose regularized estimator coincides with the posterior mean of Gaussian process regression. Building on this correspondence, we formulate Gaussian Process Dynamic Mode Decomposition, a Bayesian transfer-operator method that combines sparse variational Gaussian processes with kernel-based Koopman and Perron--Frobenius operator approximation. The resulting framework provides a principled route to uncertainty quantification, scalable sparse approximations, and data-adaptive dictionary learning for prediction and spectral analysis. Additionally, the model-selection formulation naturally gives rise to a forward--backward operator structure, which establishes a connection between Bayesian transfer-operator learning and time-lagged canonical correlation analysis.

papers.title: Simultaneous Learning and Optimization via Misspecified Saddle Point Problems
papers.abstract: We study a class of misspecified saddle point (SP) problems, where the optimization objective depends on an unknown parameter that must be learned concurrently from data. Unlike existing studies that assume parameters are fully known or pre-estimated, our framework integrates optimization and learning into a unified formulation, enabling a more flexible problem class. To address this setting, we propose two algorithms based on the accelerated primal-dual (APD) by Hamedani & Aybat 2021. In particular, we first analyze the naive extension of the APD method by directly substituting the evolving parameter estimates into the primal-dual updates; then, we design a new learning-aware variant of the APD method that explicitly accounts for parameter dynamics by adjusting the momentum updates. Both methods achieve a provable convergence rate of $\mathcal{O}(\log K / K)$, while the learning-aware approach attains a tighter $\mathcal{O}(1)$ constant and further benefits from an adaptive step-size selection enabled by a backtracking strategy. Furthermore, we extend the framework to problems where the learning problem admits multiple optimal solutions, showing that our modified algorithm for a structured setting achieves an $\mathcal{O}(1/\sqrt{K})$ rate. To demonstrate practical impact, we evaluate our methods on a misspecified portfolio optimization problem and show superior empirical performance compared to state-of-the-art algorithms.
papers.comments: Accepted for publication in the Journal of Computational Optimization and Algorithms

papers.title: General coupling-based f-divergence diagnostics for Markov chain Monte Carlo
papers.abstract: A long-standing gap exists between the theoretical analysis of Markov chain Monte Carlo convergence, which is often based on statistical divergences, and the diagnostics used in practice. We introduce the first general convergence diagnostics for Markov chain Monte Carlo based on a broad class of f-divergence, allowing users to directly monitor, among others, the Kullback-Leibler and the chi-squared divergences as well as the total variation distance. Our approach rests on a coupling-based 'weight harmonization' scheme that produces direct, computable, and consistent importance weights for interacting Markov chains with respect to their target distribution. Beyond their use as convergence diagnostics, these weights give unbiased estimates of the Radon-Nikodym derivative between the un-normalized target and the distribution of the current iterate, a richer object than the convergence bounds alone, with natural applications to importance-weighted inference. We show how such weightings can provide asymptotic upper bounds to any f-divergence, prove that these bounds converge to zero as the chains approach stationarity, and demonstrate that, while more conservative than existing coupling-based total variation estimators, our method remains a practical and broadly applicable diagnostic tool.
papers.comments: Significantly revised manuscript including new nonasymptotic bounds

papers.title: A fast and rigorous numerical tool to measure length-scale artifacts in molecular simulations
papers.abstract: The two-sided Bogoliubov inequality for classical and quantum many-body systems is a theorem that provides rigorous bounds on the free-energy cost of partitioning a given system into two or more independent subsystems. This theorem motivates the definition of a quality factor which directly quantifies the degree of statistical-mechanical consistency achieved by a given simulation box size. A major technical merit of the theorem is that, for systems with two-body interactions and a known radial distribution function, the quality factor can be computed by evaluating just three six-dimensional integrals. We present a numerical algorithm for computing the quality factor and demonstrate its consistency with respect to results in the literature obtained from simulations performed at different box sizes.
papers.comments: 29 pages, 6 figures. To be published in Commun. Appl. Math. Comput. Sci., see https://msp.org/soon/coming.php?jpath=camcos

papers.title: Sparse Modular Forms, Lattices, and Codes
papers.abstract: Motivated by sparseness conditions for holographic CFTs, we investigate sparseness of modular forms, lattices, and codes. For this we investigate the free energy of such objects as their weight, dimension or size goes to infinity. We construct families of modular forms that are sparse, such as the Eisenstein series $E_{2k}(τ)$. We then investigate lattices that come from codes and introduce a sparseness condition for such lattices. We investigate the limit of lattices constructed from self-dual Reed-Muller codes and prove that they are sparse in this sense.
papers.comments: 21 pages. v2: After publication, we found a reference that allowed us to prove sparseness of Reed-Muller code lattices. We added section 4.4 explaining this

papers.title: Improving Matrix Exponential for Generative AI Flows: A Taylor-Based Approach Beyond Paterson--Stockmeyer
papers.abstract: The matrix exponential is a fundamental operator in scientific computing and system simulation, with applications ranging from control theory and quantum mechanics to modern generative machine learning. While Padé approximants combined with scaling and squaring have long served as the standard, recent Taylor-based methods, which utilize polynomial evaluation schemes that surpass the classical Paterson--Stockmeyer technique, offer superior accuracy and reduced computational complexity. This paper presents an optimized Taylor-based algorithm for the matrix exponential, specifically designed for the high-throughput requirements of generative AI flows. We provide a rigorous error analysis and develop a dynamic selection strategy for the Taylor order and scaling factor to minimize computational effort under a prescribed error tolerance. Extensive numerical experiments demonstrate that our approach provides significant acceleration and maintains high numerical stability compared to existing state-of-the-art implementations. These results establish the proposed method as a highly efficient tool for large-scale generative modeling.
papers.comments: 52 pages, 4 figures. Revised version: added new theoretical results, sharper error analysis, additional numerical experiments, benchmarking on modern GPU hardware, comparisons with standard library implementations, and validation of generative model quality

papers.title: Auto-differentiable data assimilation: Co-learning of states, dynamics, and filtering algorithms
papers.abstract: Data assimilation algorithms estimate the state of a dynamical system from partial observations, where the successful performance of these algorithms hinges on costly parameter tuning and on employing an accurate model for the dynamics. This paper introduces a framework for jointly learning the state, dynamics, and parameters of filtering algorithms in data assimilation through a process we refer to as auto-differentiable filtering. The framework leverages a theoretically motivated loss function that enables learning from partial, noisy observations via gradient-based optimization using auto-differentiation. We further demonstrate how several well-known data assimilation methods can be learned or tuned within this framework. To underscore the versatility of auto-differentiable filtering, we perform experiments on dynamical systems spanning multiple scientific domains, such as the Clohessy-Wiltshire equations from aerospace engineering, the Lorenz-96 system from atmospheric science, the generalized Lotka-Volterra equations from systems biology, and the two-layer quasi-geostrophic model from geophysical fluid dynamics. Finally, we provide guidelines for practitioners to customize our framework according to their observation model, accuracy requirements, and computational budget.

papers.title: Directional Confusions Reveal Divergent Inductive Biases Through Rate-Distortion Geometry in Human and Machine Vision
papers.abstract: Humans and modern vision models can reach similar classification accuracy while making systematically different kinds of mistakes -- differing not in how often they err, but in who gets mistaken for whom and in which direction. We show that these directional confusions reveal distinct inductive biases that are invisible to accuracy alone. Using matched human and deep vision model responses on a natural-image categorization task under 12 perturbation types, we quantify asymmetry in confusion matrices and link it to the shape of the information-error trade-off. We characterize this trade-off geometry using three signatures extracted from the rate-distortion (RD) frontier: slope beta, curvature kappa and efficiency (AUC). We find that humans exhibit broad but weak asymmetries, whereas deep vision models show sparser, stronger directional collapses. Robustness training reduces global asymmetry but fails to recover the human-like breadth-strength profile of graded similarity. Mechanistic simulations further show that different asymmetry organizations shift the RD frontier in opposite directions, even when matched for performance. Together, these results position directional confusions and RD geometry as compact, interpretable signatures of inductive bias under distribution shift.

papers.title: Adequate Losses via Quantitative Linear Logic
papers.abstract: As neural components are increasingly embedded in existing symbolic software -- including safety-critical systems -- the question arises of how to specify and enforce the safety of the newly introduced neural parts. Unlike traditional logical specifications, these must be amenable not only to the standard Boolean interpretation, but also to training and optimisation. The latter calls for a quantitative interpretation of the logical syntax, subject to further requirements such as smoothness and differentiability. Moreover, the qualitative and quantitative sides of the logic must share a unifying proof-theoretic and categorical semantics. Finally, the new logic should link cleanly to the substructural and program logics that underpin the verification of existing symbolic programs. In this paper, we present a logic that ticks all of these boxes. We introduce a family of calculi, $p$QLL, indexed by a hardness degree $p$, prove a cut-elimination theorem for them, and establish completeness with respect to enriched residuated `soft' lattices. At $p = \infty$, $p$QLL reduces to multiplicative additive linear logic (MALL), and provability in $p$QLL converges to provability in MALL as $p \to \infty$. We express optimisation objectives in the syntax of this logic and prove the quantitative adequacy of neuro-symbolic loss functions -- a result that has eluded the neuro-symbolic machine learning community for nearly a decade.
papers.comments: Numerous tweaks and small corrections. To appear at POPL 2027

papers.title: Match classification in the last round of four-team round-robin tournaments
papers.abstract: Classification of matches played in the last rounds of sports competitions is a well-established tool for evaluating tournament designs. Our paper offers the first comparison of deterministic and probabilistic match classification models by analysing the most prominent example of four-team round-robin competitions, the group stage of the FIFA World Cup. We show that both models are highly relevant in practice: all (four) deterministic and (six) probabilistic match types occurred in the 2014 and 2018 FIFA World Cups, respectively. The probabilistic model, which accounts for the relative benefits of attacking and defending, provides a deeper insight; for instance, the competitive matches from the deterministic approach can be of any of the six probabilistic types. Therefore, the probabilistic model is used to decompose the impact of three reforms introduced in the 2026 FIFA World Cup: the expansion to 48 teams, the modified qualification rules, and head-to-head tie-breakers.

papers.title: Express Language Modeling
papers.abstract: We introduce a new tool, Express, for converting a non-causal attention approximation into a causal approximation with matching approximation guarantees. When combined with the state-of-the-art Thinformer approximation, Express improves upon the best known causal attention guarantees, delivering $\log^{3/2}(n)/s$ approximation error with only $O(s)$ memory and $O(s^2 \log^2(n))$ compression overhead for a sequence of length $n$. We pair these developments with an efficient I/O-aware Triton implementation, demonstrate substantial speedups over FlashAttention 2, and use Express to overcome four resource bottlenecks in the language modeling pipeline: long-context prefill, KV cache compression, long-form memory-constrained decoding, and long-form compute-constrained decoding.

papers.title: Quantum optimal control of steady orbits
papers.abstract: Periodically driven dissipative systems can settle into steady orbits - fixed infinite loops on their dynamical manifolds. In quantum mechanics, steady orbits occur in cooling engines, lasers and masers, precision metrology devices, and magnetic resonance. Steady orbits and stroboscopic steady states are a promising target for quantum optimal control, but the numerical complexity is prohibitive: infinite loops defeat state-of-the-art algorithms that use explicit numerical propagation in the time domain. We report a solution to this problem and introduce a numerically efficient quantum optimal control algorithm for steady orbits. We use this algorithm to design microwave pulse sequences that dynamically polarise nuclear spins and enhance their magnetic resonance signals, while taking into account instrumental distortions. Improved performance relative to leading current methods is demonstrated experimentally.

papers.title: Risk-Aware Quantile Learning for Personalized Dynamic Treatment Regimes
papers.abstract: Sequential clinical decision-making often involves more than maximizing average efficacy. Clinicians may need to simultaneously optimize clinically relevant tails of the outcome distribution, control treatment-related risk, and choose among multiple treatment options. Existing quantile dynamic treatment regime (DTR) methods capture distributional features of treatment outcomes but remain largely restricted to efficacy-only objectives and binary treatments. To address these limitations, we propose Risk-Aware Quantile Dynamic Treatment Regimes (RQDTR), a unified framework that optimizes a prespecified quantile of the cumulative potential outcome while explicitly incorporating treatment-related risk. We also develop an angle-based formulation for jointly learning decision rules across multiple treatment categories. Our framework includes three interpretable subclasses: efficacy-only quantile learning, constraint-based learning with population-level risk control, and utility-based learning through a composite benefit-risk utility. Theoretically, we establish identification and oracle equivalence, surrogate and estimator consistency under increasing quadratic penalties, asymptotic risk feasibility, and finite-sample performance error bounds. Extensive simulation studies and applications to All of Us major depressive disorder and MIMIC-III sepsis data demonstrate that RQDTR improves tail-oriented efficacy and achieves more favorable benefit-risk trade-offs than existing quantile DTR methods.
papers.comments: An earlier version of this work was accepted at STAI-X 2026

papers.title: Heuristic Lookahead Distillation Protocol Search
papers.abstract: Bipartite qubit entanglement distillation is the process of converting noisy ebits into pure ebits using only local operations and classical communication. This is a core operation for quantum repeaters, enabling such crucial tasks as long-distance quantum communication and distributed quantum computing. In this work, we introduce a method for searching for entanglement distillation protocols and, using this technique, distil qubit Werner states at a higher rate than could be achieved using previously discovered protocols. In particular, we demonstrate the advantage of our new distillation strategy by improving the best known lower bound for the two-way-assisted quantum capacity of the qubit depolarising channel across a wide range of channel parameters, making progress in one of the long-standing problems of quantum information theory.

papers.title: Novel lump solutions of the modified Kadomtsev--Petviashvili-I equation
papers.abstract: We apply the generalized long-wave limit method with spectral perturbations to construct second-order two- and three-lump solutions and third-order three-, four-, five-, and six-lump solutions of the modified Kadomtsev--Petviashvili-I equation. We determine the long-time positions and amplitudes of these degenerate lumps and show that their anomalous scattering produces asymptotic amplitude corrections that differ from those in the Kadomtsev--Petviashvili-I equation.
papers.comments: v2: added new results and updated figures

papers.title: Multiparameter Quantum Affine Spaces and the Scalene Yang--Baxter Equation
papers.abstract: We construct representation-independent families of solutions of the non-braided scalene Yang--Baxter equation from quadratic noncommutative algebras. Beginning with two anticommuting generators, we obtain a continuous deformation in terms of quantum-plane algebras and extend the construction to an arbitrary number of generators. In the latter case the scalene Yang--Baxter relation fixes the multiparameter exchange matrix to an exact multiplicative form, thereby selecting a distinguished subclass of multiparameter quantum affine spaces. We construct finite-dimensional realizations using singular matrices and finite Heisenberg--Weyl operators, as well as infinite-dimensional realizations in terms of bilateral weighted shifts and multiplicative-shift operators. The explicit realizations are generically weakly purely scalene: their individual constituent operators do not satisfy the ordinary constant non-braided Yang--Baxter equation. For selected finite-dimensional realizations, we additionally establish strong purity by obstructing a generic common meromorphic Yang--Baxter parametrization, even up to consistent invertible local similarities and nonzero scalar rescalings. These results provide a representation-independent algebraic framework for constructing scalene triples and a starting point for investigating their possible applications to quantum integrability.
papers.comments: 22 pages + Appendices + References ; v2 24 pages + Appendices + References, Published version

papers.title: A Theory of Information Architecture for Networked Decisions: Freshness, Locality, and Coordination
papers.abstract: A broader view of a network can help agents coordinate, but collecting that view takes time. When is a fresh local observation more useful than an older view of the whole network, and when should an agent look only partway across it? We study agents that repeatedly minimize a shared quadratic cost in an environment that evolves independently of their actions. An information architecture specifies what each agent observes and how old those observations are. Each agent uses a synchronized neighborhood snapshot, so extending its scope also ages the nearby readings used in the decision. We assume that the optimal action with complete information is affine in the state, and that the conditional mean of the current state equals the old state scaled by a common exponential decay factor. Using the classical Marschak--Radner decomposition, we derive the delay threshold beyond which fresh local information outperforms a complete but older global view. This comparison allows non-Gaussian states and nonlinear decision rules. We then determine how far an agent should look by balancing the benefit of additional observations against their greater age. In a Gaussian spatial model on a line, we derive the optimal observation radius: looking beyond the local node pays only when information travels more than twice the spatial correlation length in one coherence time. The preferred information architecture also depends on the decision being made. On a fixed 64-node ring, increasing only the reach of the decision weights from 0.7 to 6 hops shifts the optimal observation radius from one to five hops.
papers.comments: 32 pages, 6 figures. Manuscript source and complete reproduction materials are available at https://github.com/ANRGUSC/TINA

papers.title: Improved lower bound for the two-way-assisted quantum capacity of the bosonic thermal-loss channel
papers.abstract: The bosonic thermal-loss channel is a fundamental model for quantum communication. This Gaussian channel models the transmission of bosonic systems subject to both loss and thermal noise. It describes many practical systems, including optical fibres, waveguides and free-space links, where background thermal noise is significant. Determining the channel's two-way-assisted quantum capacity, the maximum rate at which quantum information can be transmitted reliably through the channel with two-way classical assistance, remains an open problem. Here, we improve upon the best known lower bound for this capacity for a wide range of channel parameters. We achieve this by combining an improved qubit-bosonic distribution technique with a recently introduced technique for discovering entanglement distillation protocols.

papers.title: Exact anomalous current fluctuations in the strong-anisotropy limit of the XXZ chain
papers.abstract: We study spin-current fluctuations of the folded XXZ chain, which describes the strong-anisotropy limit of the XXZ chain. We obtain an exact expression for the moment-generating function of the time-integrated spin current at infinite temperature. A long-time asymptotic analysis establishes that the rescaled time-integrated current converges to a non-Gaussian distribution described by the M-Wright function. The derivation relies on a nonlocal map to the one-dimensional t-0 model and its exact spin-charge separation. By extending this approach, we also show that the dynamical correlation function of the spins summed over two adjacent sites exhibits a diffusive Gaussian profile at long times.

papers.title: A commuting operator self-test for exact entanglement embezzlement
papers.abstract: We show that the optimal commuting operator correlation for a variant of Coladangelo's two-player generalized nonlocal game, based on the embezzlement of entanglement, is a commuting operator self-test. Our result gives the first correlation self-test for an exact entanglement embezzlement protocol in the commuting operator framework. Because the unique optimal correlation necessitates the exact embezzlement of entanglement, the correlation is unrealizable using quantum tensor-product models, even if the local spaces are allowed to be infinite dimensional. Our proof relies on Harris' unique abstract state characterization of exact embezzlement of entanglement involving Cuntz algebras.

papers.title: Tiling 3D Space by (Translates of) a Single Polycube is Undecidable
papers.abstract: We prove co-RE-completeness, and thus undecidability, of the following problem: given a single (connected) polycube, decide whether it tiles 3D Euclidean space by translations. The same result holds if we also allow rotations and/or reflections. We reduce from Wang tiling using the decorated two-prime Sudoku construction of Greenfeld and Tao and a cyclic encoding adapted from OpenAI's 3D aperiodic tile, and apply a reduction of Kim to make the prototile connected (via faces). Dimension three is optimal: translational monotiling is known to be decidable in $\mathbb{Z}^2$ and for a single (possibly disconnected) polyomino in $\mathbb{R}^2$.
papers.comments: 10 pages, 2 figures, 2 tables, 15 snippets. Added rotation/reflection results and corresponding table

papers.title: Symbolic-Permutation-Based Direct Sparse Jacobian Assembly for Accelerated Power-Flow Analysis
papers.abstract: The repeated assembly of the sparse Jacobian matrix constitutes a primary computational bottleneck in the Newton-Raphson power-flow analysis. Through an algebraic operator equivariance analysis of the Jacobian matrix, this paper formalizes the reduction process and proposes a direct sparse Jacobian assembly method based on symbolic permutation. By pre-applying the permutation to the admittance matrix during a fast one-time symbolic phase via its sparse prefix-sum property, the runtime bus-type projection overhead and indirect mapping caches are entirely eliminated. Consequently, complex Jacobian differentiation and global matrix assembly fuse into a single operation, yielding a single-pass, branchless algorithm that streams values directly into contiguous memory. The proposed algorithm is implemented in the open-source RustPower solver. Benchmarks on IEEE test systems and PEGASE 9241 demonstrate that the proposed assembly is 28.1-37.9 times faster than the MATPOWER-style baseline and 8.9-9.7 times faster than the in-house Schäfer-Braun-inspired assembly (V1); on PEGASE 9241, it outperforms optimized traditional C++ assembly routines by 3.72 times in cold construction and 2.59 times across iterations. End-to-end, the iteration-loop solve time with KLU is 1.16-1.97 times faster than the native C++ LightSim2Grid and up to 95.5 times faster than pandapower, while leaving numerical results and convergence behavior unchanged. The method extends directly to general problems where a sparse Jacobian inherits its structure from a static network operator, including transient stability analysis, EMT simulation, and OPF Hessian assembly.

papers.title: Some complete $ω$-powers of a one-counter language in the difference hierarchy
papers.abstract: Fix a finite alphabet $Σ$ having at least two letters, and natural numbers $n,k\geq 1$. We denote by $D_n(\mathbfΠ^0_k)$ the class of differences of $n$ subsets of the Cantor space $Σ^ω$ in $\mathbfΠ^0_k$, and by $D^-_n(\mathbfΠ^0_k)$ the class of complements of sets in $D_n(\mathbfΠ^0_k)$. We prove, for any natural numbers $n,k\geq 1$, the existence of a finite alphabet $Σ$ having at least two letters and a finitary language $U_{n,k}$ over $Σ$ accepted by a one-counter automaton such that the $ω$-power $$U_{n,k}^\infty:=\{ w_0w_1\cdots\inΣ^ω\mid\forall i\inω~~w_i\in U_{n,k}\}$$ is $D_{2n-1}(\mathbfΠ^0_k)$-complete. We also prove a conditional result for the dual classes $D^-_{2n}(\mathbfΠ^0_k)$: under the assumption that there exists a finitary language $V_{n,3}$ accepted by a one-counter automaton, such that its $ω$-power $V_{n,3}^\infty$ is $D^-_{2n}(\mathbfΠ^0_3)$-complete, there would also exist, for any integer $k > 3$, a finitary language $V_{n,k}$ accepted by a one-counter automaton, such that its $ω$-power $V_{n,k}^\infty$ is $D^-_{2n}(\mathbfΠ^0_k)$-complete. Finally we add another conditionnal result about Wadge degrees of rational $\mathbfΔ^0_2$ omega powers, which completes the recent results of [FGL26].

papers.title: Fer expansion of driven spins: closed-form recursion and no-go theorems for termination
papers.abstract: The Fer expansion factorizes the propagator of a driven quantum system into exponentials of time-integrated effective Hamiltonians, which govern the evolution left over by the previous factors. Every truncation is unitary, and adding a factor squares the size of the remainder, but each effective Hamiltonian is an infinite series of nested commutators of the previous one. For $\mathfrak{su}(2)$, in every representation, from qubits to spins of any dimension, we represent the effective Hamiltonians by time-dependent vectors in $\mathbb{R}^3$ and resum this series exactly. The result is a closed map from one vector to the next, in which the infinite series reduces to the previous vector crossed once and twice with its time integral, weighted by elementary functions. Using this map, we address the question of when the expansion can be stopped after finitely many factors. This is possible whenever the leftover evolution is known in closed form, for instance when the effective Hamiltonian commutes with itself at all times or precesses about a fixed axis with constant angular velocity. We prove that, for real-analytic drives, neither happens beyond the first factor unless the first exponential is already exact. Stopping the expansion therefore yields no new exactly solvable drives.
papers.comments: 9 pages, 1 figure; title and abstract revised to communicate the results more clearly; introduction and conclusion improved as well;

papers.title: Resurgence and Modularity in the First Painlevé Equation
papers.abstract: For the first Painlevé equation, we relate three nonlinear Stokes maps associated with a full turn around infinity to modular transformations of the two-parameter tau function through the identity $\boldsymbol S_π\circ\boldsymbol S_0\circ \boldsymbol S_{-π}=\mathsf S\circ\mathsf T$. Here the subscripts label Borel directions, while $\mathsf S$ and $\mathsf T$ denote the modular generators. Working under the analytic assumptions of the topological recursion and exact WKB constructions, we compare Stokes multipliers of the associated isomonodromy system while tracking the homology basis of its elliptic spectral curve under rotations of the independent variable.
